validation.notes: Written from general knowledge of the default broadcast scoreboard and match-facts screen. Not yet checked against live captures of the current edition; scoreboard reading and zone estimates must be validated before this pack is marked community or verified.

capture.notes: Use the default broadcast (or tele-broadcast) camera with the scoreboard visible. Other cameras reduce zone accuracy.

playerContext.label: Your side on the scoreboard
playerContext.help: The home team is shown on the left of the scoreboard.

playerContext.label: Your team (as shown on the scoreboard)
playerContext.help: Optional: the 3-letter abbreviation, so the recogniser can tell your goals from the opponent's.

playerContext.label: Your radar colour
playerContext.help: Your team's dots on the radar (Settings > Game Settings > Visual: User Radar Colour). Set yours and the opponent's to two different strong colours, Blue and Red work best. At Default the radar uses kit colours, so similar kits can look the same; Black cannot be told from the dark radar.

playerContext.label: Opponent's radar colour
playerContext.help: The opponent's dots on the radar (Opponent Radar Colour). Pick a colour far from yours: Red against Blue, or Orange against Purple.

vision.purpose: EA SPORTS FC match on the broadcast camera. Read the scoreboard (top-left: home abbreviation, home score, away score, away abbreviation, match clock). Recognise goals (goal celebration, GOAL graphic, or a goal replay marked REPLAY), clear losses of possession by the player's team, and the end-of-match statistics screen. The player's side and team are given in the context; left and right on the pitch are always from the perspective of the team defending that goal, looking out at the pitch. For a goal against the player, also name the first defensive mistake the replay shows, if any.

events.label: Goal (seen)
events.description: A goal is being celebrated, a GOAL graphic is shown, or a goal replay is playing. Report who scored relative to the player, where the final shot was taken from (zone in the goal area of the goal it went into), and how the goal was created if it is visible.

How the chance was created, only if visible in the replay.

events.description: In this frame the player's team clearly loses the ball to the opponent (interception, tackle, or a misplaced pass reaching an opponent).

zones.label: Where the goal came from
zones.description: Where the final shot was taken from, relative to the goal it went into. Left and right are from the defending goalkeeper's point of view, looking out at the pitch. 'Inside the box' means the penalty area.

zones.label: Pitch third
zones.description: Thirds of the pitch relative to the player's team: defensive third is nearest the player's own goal. Left and right are from the player's team's attacking direction.

concepts.title: Hold your defensive shape
concepts.summary: Many goals come from defenders pulled out of position. Containing the ball carrier while your line stays compact usually concedes fewer clear chances than chasing.
good: Jockey and contain the ball carrier
Switch to the defender covering the passing lane
Keep the back line compact
bad: Pulling a centre-back out to press high
Sprinting at the ball carrier and getting beaten
Leaving the space behind a full-back open

concepts.title: Covering crosses and cutbacks
concepts.summary: When the ball goes wide, the most dangerous space is often the penalty spot area for a cutback, not just the near post.
good: Track runners into the box
Cover the cutback zone when the ball reaches the byline
bad: Ball-watching while a runner arrives unmarked
Every defender drawn to the near post

concepts.title: Lower risk near your own goal
concepts.summary: Losing the ball in your own third gives the opponent a short route to goal. Simple passes or clearances under pressure reduce that risk.
good: Simple passes when pressed near your box
Clearing when no safe pass is on
bad: Risky passes across your own box
Dribbling out of defence under pressure

concepts.title: Patient build-up
concepts.summary: Recycling the ball when forward options are covered keeps possession and pass accuracy higher than forcing passes into crowded areas.
good: Switch play to the open side
Recycle to a centre-back to reset
bad: Forcing through balls into crowded areas
Long passes under pressure

concepts.title: Shot selection
concepts.summary: Shots from inside the box with space convert far more often than speculative long shots.
good: Work the ball into the box
Shoot when you have a clear sight of goal
bad: Long shots under pressure
Shooting from tight angles when a pass is on

prohibitedAdvice: Exploits, glitches, or anything against EA's rules
Anything about the opponent that is not visible on the player's own screen
Live instructions during online or competitive matches

playbook.title: Jockey first, tackle second
playbook.principle: Jockey to stay goal-side and slow the attacker, and tackle only when the ball is exposed after a heavy touch or a skill move. FC 27 made jockeying faster, so containing works better than diving in.
good: About a metre of space, goal-side, steering the attacker to the touchline or a covering teammate
Tackling after a heavy touch
bad: Diving in early
Biting on fake shots
Several tackle attempts in a row
signals: Replay: your defender lunges and the attacker goes past them
playbook.fix: Hold jockey and tackle only when the ball comes away from the attacker's feet.

sources.title: FC 27 Pitch Notes: gameplay deep dive (EA)

playbook.title: Switch to the receiver before the pass
playbook.principle: In FC 27, AI defenders reach less far for interceptions than a defender you control. Take the defender who will face the threat before the ball arrives.
good: Flicking the right stick to the defender in the target lane
Already controlling them when the through ball is struck
bad: Cycling the switch button after the pass
Switching while the ball is in the air
signals: Replay: your controlled player arrives late; an AI defender stands still as the ball goes past
playbook.fix: Pick the next defender with the right stick as the passer shapes to play.

sources.title: FC 27 Pitch Notes: gameplay deep dive (EA)
Defending tips from RBLZ_Levyfinn (World Championship runner-up)

playbook.title: Defend with the midfield, keep the centre-backs as the safety net
playbook.principle: Run back and press with the defensive midfielder first and leave the back line in shape. Take a centre-back only once the midfield screen is beaten.
good: Defensive midfielder between the ball and the striker's lane
Teammate contain used with the midfielder
bad: Controlling a centre-back at halfway
Contain with your main defender, dragging them out
signals: Replay: your controlled centre-back 20 m or more ahead of the line when the move starts
playbook.fix: Defend through midfield with the defensive midfielder and take a centre-back only in the final third.

sources.title: How to defend in FC 26, NealGuides
Getting destroyed on defence in FC 27, Operation Sports

playbook.title: Do not pull centre-backs out of the line
playbook.principle: Taking a centre-back out of the line opens a gap the AI does not cover and invites balls in behind.
good: Centre-backs level with each other
Midfielders stepping out to the ball carrier
bad: A centre-back chasing a dropping striker
A centre-back pulled wide to a winger
signals: Replay: a wide gap between the centre-backs with the scorer running through it
playbook.fix: Let a midfielder engage a dropping forward and keep the centre-back in the line.

sources.title: Defending tips from RBLZ_Levyfinn (World Championship runner-up)
How to defend in FC 27, FIFA UTeam

playbook.title: Tap the press, do not hold it
playbook.principle: Holding second-man press drags AI teammates out of shape. In FC 27, Team Press does nothing in your defensive third.
good: Short taps to force a backward pass
Pressing from midfield
bad: Holding contain for the whole possession
Relying on Team Press near your own box
signals: A simple one-two beats two of your players at once
playbook.fix: Tap to press briefly, then release and recover your shape.

sources.title: Getting destroyed on defence in FC 27, Operation Sports

playbook.title: Protect the penalty spot and the edge of the box
playbook.principle: Cutbacks beat defenders who chase the ball toward the byline. Block the pass back inside and accept a cross from a poor angle.
good: Controlled defender between the byline carrier and the penalty spot
A midfielder recovering to the edge of the box
bad: Sprinting at the winger
Every defender collapsing onto the six-yard line
signals: Replay: scorer unmarked 10 to 18 m out after a pass back from the byline
playbook.fix: Switch to the player covering the penalty-spot lane, not the one chasing the winger.

sources.title: How to defend in FC 27, FIFA UTeam
Defending in FC 26 thread, EA Forums

playbook.title: Watch the far-post runner on crosses
playbook.principle: FC 27 crosses land in space more often, so far-post runs are more dangerous. Choose your aerial defender before the cross is struck.
good: Controlling the far-side centre-back or full-back as the winger shapes to cross
Goal-side of the runner
bad: Cycling defenders while the ball is in the air
Far-side full-back tucked too narrow
signals: Replay: header or volley at the far post with no defender within about 2 m
playbook.fix: Take the far-post defender before the cross and stand goal-side of the runner.

sources.title: FC 27 Pitch Notes: gameplay deep dive (EA)
Getting destroyed on defence in FC 27, Operation Sports

playbook.title: Set the line height for your recovery pace
playbook.principle: Tekkz and RedLac run a line height around 61 to 65, and usage data clusters near 60. If you keep getting beaten in behind, guides suggest 45 to 55, or quicker centre-backs.
good: Line height matched to your centre-backs' pace
Lowering the line after conceding in behind
bad: A line above 70 with slow centre-backs
signals: Two or more goals from balls over the top, scorer starting near halfway
playbook.fix: After conceding in behind twice, drop the line 5 to 10 points or play a quicker centre-back.

sources.title: Best FC 27 custom tactics with Tekkz and RedLac, Red Bull

playbook.title: Read and cut off through balls
playbook.principle: FC 27 through balls follow the passer's aim closely, so they are easier to read but punish late reactions. A shoulder challenge can push a runner off the ball.
good: Controlled defender on the runner's inside shoulder
Defensive midfielder in the central lane
bad: An unmarked runner splitting the line
Defender facing the ball instead of the runner
signals: Replay: one-on-one with your keeper after a through ball, scorer starting beside your last defender
playbook.fix: Before the pass, take the defender nearest the runner and match the run on their inside shoulder.

sources.title: FC 27 Pitch Notes: gameplay deep dive (EA)
Getting destroyed on defence in FC 27, Operation Sports

playbook.title: Watch full-backs that drop early
playbook.principle: Full-backs dropping early and playing attackers onside is a widely reported FC 27 issue that EA has reportedly put under review.
good: Full-back level with the centre-backs
Taking the full-back yourself when the ball goes wide
bad: A full-back 3 to 5 m deeper than the line, playing the scorer onside
signals: Replay: the offside line set by a full-back, not a centre-back
playbook.fix: Take the full-back yourself and step them up to the line when the ball is central.

playbook.title: Defend corners with your best header
playbook.principle: Pick one aerial defender early instead of switching once the ball is in the air.
good: Your tallest centre-back under control before the kick
bad: Switching mid-flight
signals: Corner goal with your controlled player outside the six-yard box
playbook.fix: Select your strongest header before the corner is taken.

playbook.title: Do not pass into pressure
playbook.principle: A ground pass is easy to intercept when a defender stands in the lane. Against a compact block, forcing the ball forward hands it back.
good: Waiting for a runner who can actually receive
Moving the ball sideways or back to reset
bad: Vertical passes into a marked striker
Passing while sprinting
signals: Interceptions in midfield with the interceptor standing in the passing lane
playbook.fix: Pass forward only when the lane is clear; otherwise recycle it back.

playbook.title: Limit lofted passes in build-up
playbook.principle: Lofted passes hang in the air and give defenders time to recover. Use them to switch play or beat a high line, not to circulate.
good: A lofted switch into space
A lofted through ball over a high line
bad: Lofted passes to a tightly marked midfielder
signals: The receiver loses the header or duel straight after a lofted pass
playbook.fix: Play on the ground unless the receiver is in clear space or the ball goes over a high line.

playbook.title: Aim through balls, do not spam them
playbook.principle: FC 27 removed most through-ball assistance, so a badly aimed ball gets intercepted.
good: Aiming at the space ahead of a runner who has started moving
Diagonal through balls
bad: Through balls into crowded areas
Releasing before the runner moves
signals: Through ball intercepted with the runner still level or behind
playbook.fix: Release the through ball after the runner's first steps, into the space ahead of them.

sources.title: FC 27 Pitch Notes: gameplay deep dive (EA)

playbook.title: Play out with a safety option
playbook.principle: Keep one safe pass back or sideways at all times; Short or Balanced build-up keeps more short options available.
good: Centre-back, defensive midfielder and full-back in a triangle
Switching sides through the centre-backs
bad: Every midfielder running forward, leaving only a long ball
Driven passes across your own box
signals: Ball lost in your own half, then a shot against within about 10 seconds
playbook.fix: Before receiving, check for a second option and use the centre-back to switch sides.

sources.title: Best FC 27 custom tactics with Tekkz and RedLac, Red Bull

playbook.title: Match risk to the zone
playbook.principle: In your own third, a turnover becomes a shot straight away, so keep it simple there. Take risks in the final third. This is a coaching rule of thumb, not a measured statistic.
good: Simple passes in your own half
Creative passes in the final third
bad: Skill moves or driven passes near your own box
signals: A goal against that starts with a turnover in your own third
playbook.fix: Keep it simple in your own third and take risks only in the opponent's third.

playbook.title: Get to the byline and pull it back
playbook.principle: Analytics research links cutbacks and passes from the area just outside the box with foot shots, which are higher quality than headers. A cutback lands behind defenders who are running back toward goal.
good: Winger reaching the byline
A runner arriving late at the penalty spot
bad: Crossing high to a lone striker
Shooting from tight angles
signals: Many crosses, few headers on target
playbook.fix: At the byline, pass back to the late runner instead of crossing high.

sources.title: Analysing crosses in Liga MX, Cambio de Juego

playbook.title: Use width and switch play
playbook.principle: When the middle is blocked, switching sides stretches a compact defence.
good: The ball reaching the far side within two or three passes
bad: Every attack through the middle
signals: High possession, few shots, turnovers in central areas
playbook.fix: After two blocked central passes, switch to the far side.

playbook.title: Low driven inside the box, finesse from an angle with space
playbook.principle: Guides rate the low driven shot as the most reliable finish inside the box. Finesse works best from an angle with space, on the stronger foot.
good: Low driven across the keeper
Finesse to the far post with space
bad: Long shots under pressure
signals: Many shots, low expected goals per shot, many blocked shots
playbook.fix: Work the ball into the box before shooting, and shoot from range only when unpressured.

sources.title: FC 27 tips from a pro, Red Bull

playbook.title: Be patient in possession
playbook.principle: Hold the ball until a runner is really available. FC 27 lets you trigger curved runs, but they stop after a short distance.
good: Circulating the ball, then a well-timed pass into space
bad: Going direct straight after every recovery
signals: Low possession with low pass accuracy
playbook.fix: Recycle the ball until a runner is moving into space.

sources.title: FC 27 Pitch Notes: gameplay deep dive (EA)
FC 27 tips from a pro, Red Bull

playbook.title: Aim crosses into space
playbook.principle: FC 27 crosses depend on your aim and power and land in space more often than on a player.
good: Crosses aimed ahead of a runner already moving
bad: Crosses into a crowd with no aim
signals: Crosses landing with no attacker near the ball
playbook.fix: Aim crosses at the runner's path, not where they are now.

sources.title: FC 27 Pitch Notes: gameplay deep dive (EA)

playbook.title: Find the first mistake in the goal replay
playbook.principle: A conceded goal usually starts with one defensive mistake well before the finish: a defender pulled out, an unmarked far-post runner, a cutback lane left open, a line broken, a full-back playing someone onside, or a turnover in your own third.
good: Naming the first mistake, not the finish
bad: Blaming the keeper or the finish every time
signals: The same first mistake behind several goals
playbook.fix: Watch each goal replay for the first defensive mistake, not the shot.

sources.title: Defending tips from RBLZ_Levyfinn (World Championship runner-up)

playbook.title: Read the match stats against simple lines
playbook.principle: Useful warning lines: pass accuracy under 75%, under about a third of shots on target, and expected goals per shot under about 0.10. These are coaching rules of thumb drawn from real-football averages, not FC data. Judge trends over ten matches.
good: Tracking pass accuracy and shot quality over ten matches
bad: Judging yourself on one match
signals: Pass accuracy under 75%; many shots with few on target
playbook.fix: Track your pass accuracy and shots on target over ten matches, not one.

playbook.title: Short, focused practice blocks
playbook.principle: FC 27 Skill Games cover passing and defending, and the Practice Arena lets you add defenders for one-on-one practice. Ten to fifteen minutes on one theme works better than long unfocused sessions.
good: A ten-minute block on jockey and tackle timing, then through-ball aiming
bad: Practising everything at once
signals: The same conceded-goal pattern across several matches
playbook.fix: Before each session, spend ten minutes on your most common conceded-goal pattern.

sources.title: Which FC 27 mode is right for you (EA)
Using the Practice Arena, Ludo Guide

playbook.title: Defending settings to check
playbook.principle: Guides disagree on settings: most suggest Tactical Defending and right-stick switching, and some suggest Auto Switching Move Assist set to None. EA has reportedly said manual defending will not be retuned, so adapting pays off.
good: Testing one setting at a time over five matches
bad: Changing several settings at once
signals: Late switching in goal replays
playbook.fix: Change one defending setting at a time and keep it for five matches.

sources.title: Manual defending in FC 27, G2A News
FC 27 defending feedback thread, EA Forums

playbook.title: Keep the lines close when defending
playbook.principle: When you defend, keep your back line and your midfield close together and keep the whole team short. Elite teams defend with roughly 10 metres between the back line and midfield. A short block leaves little room between the lines for passes into feet.
playbook.why: A Bundesliga tracking study (153 games, 2020/21) found defending teams averaged about 10 m between the defensive and midfield lines and a surface area near 790 square metres. A systematic review puts team length at roughly 31 to 46 m across phases. In FC 27 the AI no longer auto-tackles (EA deep dive), so a shape that blocks lanes matters more: AI players still screen passes even when they will not win the ball.
good: Back-line and midfield markers moving up and down together
A gap between the lines of about 10 to 15 metres
Team length under about 40 metres with the ball in your half
bad: Midfielders left high after losing the ball while the back four drops
An empty band between the lines where their number 10 can receive
signals: Radar, out of possession: the gap between your deepest defenders and your nearest midfielders is more than about 15 m, roughly a seventh of the radar's length.
Radar: your outfield markers span more than about 45 m from front to back while the opponent has the ball in your half.
Stats screen: many shots conceded from just outside your box.
playbook.fix: When the ball is in your half, pull your midfield back until it sits about ten to fifteen metres in front of your defenders.
playbook.drill: Kick-Off vs CPU: for one half, pause each time the opponent crosses halfway and check the gap between your back line and midfield on the radar.

sources.title: Is a compact organisation important for defensive success in elite soccer? (Bundesliga tracking study)

playbook.title: Press on a trigger, not all the time
playbook.principle: Step up to press when there is a clear cue: a back pass, a poor first touch, a receiver facing their own goal, or the ball going out to the touchline. Otherwise hold your shape. In FC 27, Team Press does nothing in your own defensive third, so press higher up.
playbook.why: Coaching material splits pressing into the trap, the shape that channels the ball, and the trigger, the moment to commit. Common triggers are a sideways or backward pass, a receiver with their back to goal and a poor first touch. EA's closed-beta update removed Team Press in your defensive third, and AI teammates now contain from slightly further away, so the user chooses the moment.
good: Pressing as the ball travels back to a centre-back or keeper
Closing a winger against the touchline with two players
Holding position when the receiver faces forward with space
bad: Chasing every pass with one player
Pressing a player who faces forward with two passing options
signals: Radar: the ball moves back toward their goal while your nearest marker is more than about 10 m away and closes late.
Radar: an opponent on the touchline with one of your markers near them while the second stays more than about 15 m away.
Stats screen: few tackles and interceptions, with a long Ball Recovery Time.
playbook.fix: Press when the ball goes backwards or to the touchline, and hold your shape when the receiver faces forward.
playbook.drill: Kick-Off vs CPU: press only on a back pass or a touchline ball for one half and compare Ball Recovery Time with a normal half.

sources.title: The 6 most important pressing triggers (Fussballcoach newsletter)
Pitch Notes: FC 27 Gameplay Deep Dive (EA)

playbook.title: Slide across with the ball
playbook.principle: When the ball goes to one flank, your back line and midfield should slide toward it together. The far full-back tucks in toward the centre-backs. The space you give up is the far touchline, which is the hardest place to reach with one pass.
playbook.why: Coaching guidance on low and mid blocks stresses short distances within and between lines, which means shifting together toward the ball. If the far full-back stays wide, the gap to the nearest centre-back opens a channel through the middle. FIFA's World Cup 2022 analysis ties mid-block success to compactness.
good: Four defenders spread across about 30 to 35 metres, shifted toward the ball
Far full-back level with the far post area
bad: Back four still spread across the full width while the ball is on one wing
A gap of 15 metres or more between a full-back and the nearest centre-back
signals: Radar, ball on one wing: your four defenders span more than about 45 m across the pitch, roughly two thirds of the radar's height.
Radar: more than about 15 m between a centre-back and the next defender on the ball side.
playbook.fix: When the ball goes wide, slide the whole back line toward it and keep the far full-back narrow.

sources.title: In Focus: Defending in a low block (Coaches' Voice)
Controlling the game without the ball: the mid-block and compactness (FIFA Training Centre)
Reference values for collective tactical behaviours in professional football: a systematic review (PMC)

playbook.title: Track runners from midfield
playbook.principle: Late runners from midfield arrive in the box after your defenders have picked up the strikers. A midfielder must follow that run, or a defender must take it over. FC 27 attackers read space and curve their runs, so blind-side runs are common.
playbook.why: EA says FC 27 AI attackers weigh space, defensive shape and the offside line and curve their runs in. Roles such as Box Crasher and Shadow Striker exist to make late runs. Your AI midfielders hold shape but may not follow a runner into the box, so a manual switch is often needed.
good: A midfielder following a runner all the way into the box
Switching to the midfielder nearest the runner as they start
bad: Only defenders in the box while an opponent arrives untracked from deep
Watching the ball while a runner passes behind your midfield
signals: Radar: an opponent crosses your midfield line toward the box and none of your markers is within about 3 m of them for two seconds or more.
Goal replay: the scorer started level with your midfielders and arrived unmarked.
playbook.fix: When a midfielder runs past your midfield line, switch to your nearest midfielder and follow them into the box.

sources.title: Pitch Notes: FC 27 Gameplay Deep Dive (EA)
Zonal marking: football tactics explained (Coaches' Voice)

playbook.title: Cover the near post, the far post and the spot
playbook.principle: When the ball is wide near your box, you need bodies in three places: the near post, the far post and the penalty spot. Do not let every defender collapse onto the near post. FC 27 crosses land in space more often, so the far post and the spot are danger zones.
playbook.why: StatsBomb data show almost all headers come from the central part of the box, and foot shots there convert about twice as often as headers. EA's deep dive says FC 27 crosses are delivered into space more often, with aim and power deciding where they land. Covering three zones takes away both the header and the cutback.
good: One defender near each post area and a midfielder near the penalty spot
bad: Three or more of your players within a few metres of the near post
Nobody of yours between the six-yard box and the penalty spot
signals: Radar, ball wide in your final third: three or more of your markers bunched within about 5 m of the near post, with an opponent free at the far post.
Radar: an opponent near your penalty spot, about 11 m out, with none of your markers near them.
playbook.fix: When the ball is wide near your box, put a defender on each post area and a midfielder on the penalty spot.

sources.title: How do headers compare to shots? (StatsBomb)
Pitch Notes: FC 27 Gameplay Deep Dive (EA)
In Focus: Attacking in the final third, crossing and finishing (Coaches' Voice)

playbook.title: Leave enough players behind the ball
playbook.principle: While you attack, keep a rest defence of one more player behind the ball than they have forwards up the pitch. Against two strikers that usually means two centre-backs and a holding midfielder. Then one lost pass does not become three against two.
playbook.why: Coaches' Voice describes rest defence as the players around and below the ball ready to stop counters, most often on a plus-one basis. A JSSM study found fast regains after losing the ball are the main success factor in defensive transition, which needs players close to the ball. FC 27 AI defenders will not win the ball back for you.
good: Two centre-backs plus one midfielder in your half when you attack their final third
Only one full-back joining the attack at a time
bad: Both full-backs and both central midfielders in their half at once
Two of your players against three of theirs after a turnover
signals: Radar, your attack in their final third: fewer of your markers in your own half than their forwards plus one.
Radar: both of your full-backs in the opponent's final third at the same moment.
Goal replay: the counter started with your defenders outnumbered near halfway.
playbook.fix: Before a full-back goes forward, check the radar that you still have one more defender back than they have forwards.

sources.title: Success factors in defensive transition / rest defence (Journal of Sports Science and Medicine)
Rest defence (FIFA Training Centre, Olympic tournament analysis)

playbook.title: Go forward fast when they are caught upfield
playbook.principle: When you win the ball and the opponent has players committed forward, play forward into space within a few seconds. The chance closes once their midfield recovers. If they already have six or more players behind the ball, slow down and keep it.
playbook.why: Rest-defence research shows counters are stopped by quick regains and numbers behind the ball, so the attacking side's best chance is in the first seconds. Many FC 27 lobbies defend at 95 depth (Timesaver), which leaves large space behind once a pass escapes the press. Lobbed and driven lobs reach runners quickly (FIFPlay).
good: First pass forward or into the channel within about three seconds
A runner already moving as the ball is won
bad: Turning back to a centre-back when only three opponents are goal-side
Dribbling sideways while their midfield recovers
signals: Radar, as you win the ball: four or fewer opponent markers between the ball and their goal means a counter is on.
Radar: their deepest defender is near halfway and your striker is level with them.
playbook.fix: When you win the ball with four or fewer opponents goal-side, play forward within three seconds.

sources.title: FC 27 95 depth offside trap: how to beat it (Timesaver)

playbook.title: Overload one side, then attack the other
playbook.principle: Draw their midfield and full-back to one side with short passes and extra bodies, then switch fast to your free winger or full-back on the far side. The aim is a one against one, or two against one, before they can slide across.
playbook.why: Coaches' Voice notes that a few attackers can pin several defenders and create an overload elsewhere. A switch only pays when their block is squeezed onto one side; played too early it moves the ball into a defended area. FC 27 lob types (FIFPlay) reach the far flank quickly.
good: Four or five of your players on one side, then a quick switch
A winger holding the far touchline while the ball is on the other side
bad: Switching before their block has shifted
All your attackers on the same side as the ball
signals: Radar: their defenders packed within about 25 m of the ball-side touchline and your far winger has nobody within about 10 m of them.
Radar: your far-side wide player has drifted inside, so nobody of yours holds the far touchline.
playbook.fix: Pull them to one side with short passes, then switch to the free winger on the far touchline.

playbook.title: Use the third man to beat a press
playbook.principle: When the only pass is into a marked player, play it with a third player already running into the space behind their marker. The lay-off finds the runner facing forward. FC 27's Pass and Follow and curved runs make this easier to set up.
playbook.why: Coaches' Voice explains the third-man run: draw an opponent to the ball, exchange two passes, and release a third player into the space left behind, turning two against two into an overload. FC 27 adds Pass and Follow (L1 plus R1 plus Cross, or LB plus RB plus A) and the Triggered Curved Run (FUT.GG).
good: Pass into the striker, who lays it off to an arriving midfielder
The runner moving before the second pass
bad: Passing into a marked striker with no runner near them
Starting the run after the lay-off
signals: Radar: your striker has an opponent within about 2 m and no other marker of yours is moving into the space within about 10 m of them.
Stats screen: many passes intercepted in the middle third.
playbook.fix: Before you pass into a marked player, trigger a run from a third player into the space behind their marker.

sources.title: Third-man runs: football tactics explained (Coaches' Voice)
How to do Triggered Curved Runs and Pass & Follow Runs in FC 27 (FUT.GG)

playbook.title: Beat a very high line in behind
playbook.principle: Against a very high line, the space is behind the defenders, not in front of them. Play a lobbed or driven ball into the channel as your runner starts level with the last defender. Curved runs help your forward stay onside and then bend in behind.
playbook.why: Many FC 27 lobbies use the Aggressive approach, whose default line height is 95 (FIFA Ultimate Team guide). Timesaver says the depth slider acts more literally, manual runs stop after a capped distance and through balls are less assisted, so timing the pass and the run is the counter. EA has announced no change.
good: Lobbed through pass (L1 plus Triangle, or LB plus Y) into the channel
Runner starting level with the last defender
bad: Short passes into a crowded midfield against a high press
Releasing the ball after the runner has crossed the line
signals: Radar: their deepest defender is within about 10 m of halfway, over 40 m from their own goal, while their keeper stays near their box.
Stats screen: many offsides against you.
Radar: your striker is already a couple of metres beyond their last defender when you pass.
playbook.fix: When their last defender is near halfway, play the ball over the top as your striker starts level with them.

sources.title: FC 27 95 depth offside trap: how to beat it (Timesaver)

playbook.title: Shoot from distance only with a clear lane
playbook.principle: A shot from outside the box is worth only a few hundredths of a goal on average, and a blocked one can start a counter. Shoot from range only when nobody stands between you and the goal and you are not under pressure. Otherwise work it into the box.
playbook.why: xG explainers put the average shot from outside the box near 0.036 xG and edge-of-box shots at roughly 0.05 to 0.10, against 0.3 or more inside the six-yard box. Power shots have a slow wind-up; guides advise creating space first and avoiding them in a crowded box.
good: Power or finesse shot from range with no defender in the lane
Passing into the box instead of shooting through bodies
bad: Shooting from 25 m with two defenders in the lane
Long shots when you lead and could keep the ball
signals: Radar at the shot: the ball is more than about 22 m from goal with two or more opponents between it and the goal.
Stats screen: many shots but expected goals per shot under about 0.08, with many blocked.
playbook.fix: From outside the box, shoot only when no defender stands in the line to goal.

sources.title: Expected goals part one: what is xG and how is it measured (Fantasy Football Scout)

playbook.title: Check the near post before you shoot
playbook.principle: In FC 27 a low driven shot inside the near post is a strong option when the keeper leaves a gap there, for example after stepping toward the far post. Look at the keeper before you pick the far corner every time.
playbook.why: EA's launch updates say feedback suggests low driven shots, particularly toward the near post, can be stronger than other options; EA is broadly happy with the shooting and goalkeeping balance and is monitoring. It is part of the current balance, not an exploit, and may change in a later update.
good: Low driven shot inside the near post when the keeper steps across
Varying near and far post
bad: Aiming every finish at the far corner
Shooting low driven into a keeper standing on the near post
signals: Radar: your shooter is in the box at an angle and the keeper sits nearer the far post than the near post.
Goal replays: nearly all your goals go far post while saves pile up from the same angle.
playbook.fix: At an angle in the box, look at the keeper and take the low driven shot near post when they have stepped toward the far post.

playbook.title: Cross when you have numbers in the box
playbook.principle: Before you cross, count. Cross when two of your attackers are in or arriving in the box. If the box is full of defenders, cut back or keep the ball. Use a ground cross for a late runner and a driven cross for the far post.
playbook.why: StatsBomb data show headers convert at about half the rate of foot shots from the same central areas. FC 27 crosses drop into the space you aim at rather than homing on a player (EA), so a cross into a crowded box is low value. Ground and driven ground crosses keep the finish on the foot.
good: A ground cross (Square twice, or X twice) to a runner arriving at the near post
Crossing when two attackers attack different zones
bad: A high cross into three defenders and one attacker
Crossing from deep with nobody yet in the box
signals: Radar, wide player in the final third: one of your markers in the box against three or more of theirs.
Radar: two or more of your markers arriving in the box on different lines: a good moment to deliver.
Stats screen: many crosses, few shots on target.
playbook.fix: Cross only when two of your attackers are in or arriving in the box; otherwise cut back or keep the ball.

sources.title: How do headers compare to shots? (StatsBomb)
Pitch Notes: FC 27 Gameplay Deep Dive (EA)
FC 27 Controls guide for PS5, Xbox and PC (Driffle)
In Focus: Attacking in the final third, crossing and finishing (Coaches' Voice)

playbook.title: Make two against one on the flank
playbook.principle: Get a second player beyond or inside your winger so their full-back faces two. An overlap runs outside the winger; an underlap runs inside them. Whichever way the full-back turns, one of your players is free. Send only one full-back at a time.
playbook.why: Two-against-one combinations beat a single defender without relying on a dribble. FC 27 lets you trigger the run with L1 or LB, a Triggered Curved Run, or Pass and Follow (FUT.GG). Coaches' Voice defines overlaps and underlaps as runs around or inside the ball carrier.
good: A full-back running outside the winger as they carry inside
A central midfielder underlapping into the channel
bad: A winger alone against two defenders
Both full-backs overlapping at once
signals: Radar: your winger and one other marker are both near their full-back, with no second defender within about 10 m.
Radar: your winger alone against two defenders on the flank.
playbook.fix: When your winger faces one defender, send a second player past them on the outside or the inside.

How to do Triggered Curved Runs and Pass & Follow Runs in FC 27 (FUT.GG)

playbook.title: Plan the corner before you take it
playbook.principle: In FC 27 your attackers do not move to the best spot for you. Pick a target zone, deliver, then use Avoidance to slip your marker and Shielding to hold the spot before the header. If the box is crowded, take it short.
playbook.why: EA's deep dive gives a brief window after delivery to control attackers in the box. Avoidance (hold R1 or RB) gets through crowds and Shielding (hold L2 or LT) holds position (FUT.GG). Set-piece tactics on D-pad Up let you add or remove runners and send players near or far post (Pro Clubs HQ).
good: Delivering to the zone your best header starts closest to
A short corner when they pack the box
bad: Delivering, then waiting for the AI to attack the ball
The same cross into the same crowd every time
signals: Radar at a corner: eight or more opponent markers in the box against four of yours suggests a short corner.
Stats screen: many corners and no shots from them.
playbook.fix: Choose a zone before the corner, then use Avoidance and Shielding to get your best header there.
playbook.drill: Kick-Off vs CPU: take ten corners to the same zone, five with Avoidance and five without, and count headers on target.

sources.title: How to use Avoidance and Shielding in FC 27 corner kicks (FUT.GG)
Pitch Notes: FC 27 Gameplay Deep Dive (EA)

playbook.title: Keep cover back at your corners
playbook.principle: When you take a corner, keep at least two players back and one on the edge of the box for the clearance. A cleared corner against a team with a fast forward left up can become a goal against within seconds.
playbook.why: The rest-defence idea applies at set pieces too: Coaches' Voice describes the rest-defence unit outnumbering the opponents' forwards by one. FC 27 set-piece tactics let you add or remove runners, so you choose how many go forward (Pro Clubs HQ).
good: Two defenders near halfway against one forward
One midfielder on the edge of the box
bad: Everyone in the box except the keeper
Nobody on the edge to win the clearance
signals: Radar at your corner: fewer of your markers in your own half than their forwards plus one.
Radar: none of your markers on the edge of their box, outside the area, when the corner is struck.
playbook.fix: Before a corner, use set-piece tactics to keep two defenders back and one player on the edge of the box.

sources.title: The most exciting improvements in EA FC 27 (Red Bull)

playbook.title: Shoot direct only when the angle is there
playbook.principle: Take a direct free kick when you are central and close enough for your taker to get over or round the wall. From wide or deep, a cross or a short routine is usually better. Change your power with the distance instead of using the same amount every time.
playbook.why: Guides describe FC 27 free kicks as the FC 24 framework: place the reticle, drag a marker across the ball for spin and lift, then hold for power. EA names Free Kick Accuracy, Curve and Shot Power as the taker attributes. Operation Sports says the common mistake is using the same power from every distance.
good: Your best Free Kick Accuracy and Curve player on central free kicks
Crossing from wide free kicks into a planned zone
bad: Shooting from wide angles into the wall
Full power from every distance
signals: Free kick taken from a wide angle that hits the wall or goes wide.
Shot sails over the bar after holding most of the power bar from close range.
playbook.fix: Shoot direct only from central positions near the box, and set the power to match the distance.

sources.title: How to take free kicks in EA SPORTS FC (EA Help)
Score from every distance with these EA FC 27 free kick techniques (Operation Sports)

playbook.title: Pick your spot early on penalties
playbook.principle: Choose your spot before the run-up, aim low toward a corner and keep the power to around half the bar. Vary your side across matches. Composure and the Penalties attribute matter more than Finishing.
playbook.why: An FC 27 guide advises a low corner, no more than about half the bar and committing before the run-up, and says Composure and Penalties matter more than Finishing. Earlier-edition guides add that varying height, side and power keeps keepers guessing.
good: Low to a corner with moderate power
Choosing a taker with high Composure and Penalties
bad: Holding the power bar near full
Going to the same side every time
signals: A penalty missed high after a nearly full power bar.
Your last few penalties all went to the same side.
playbook.fix: Pick a low corner before the run-up and stop the power bar around halfway.

sources.title: EA FC 27 Free Kicks Guide, incl. penalties (Elocarry)
EA Sports FC 24: how to take penalties (WePC)

playbook.title: Keep the ball when you are ahead late
playbook.principle: When you lead late on, possession is your defence. Circulate in midfield and your own half, take the safe pass, and when you do go forward take the ball toward their corner flag. Avoid long shots and risky through balls that hand it back.
playbook.why: Each lost ball late on is a chance for them, and with FC 27's weaker AI defending, long spells without the ball are harder to survive. Guides advise slowing the tempo and protecting the ball when leading.
good: Short passes and switches with no forward risk
Shielding the ball near their corner flag in the last minutes
bad: Through balls into a crowded box at 85 minutes when one goal up
Long shots with time running down
signals: Score clock shows you ahead after about 75 minutes, and the radar shows the ball in your final third with only one of your markers near it.
Stats screen: your possession falls in the second half while you lead.
playbook.fix: When you lead late, keep the ball in midfield and take it to their corner rather than forcing a forward pass.

sources.title: EA FC 27 guide and tips (Red Bull)
Pitch Notes: FC 27 Gameplay Deep Dive (EA)

playbook.title: Change the plan with the score and the clock
playbook.principle: Have three saved tactics ready: normal, protecting a lead, and chasing. D-pad Left opens My Tactics and D-pad Right opens Tactical Focus. Protect a late lead by dropping the line and adding a holding player. Chase by adding a striker and pushing the line up.
playbook.why: FC 27 keeps up to five saved custom tactics on D-pad Left and Tactical Focus (Default, Attacking, Defending) on D-pad Right, which shifts build-up and compatible role focuses without editing the saved tactic. Line height bands: Deep 1-30, High 61-90, Aggressive 91-100.
good: Switching to a lead-protection tactic around 80 minutes when ahead
Adding a striker and Attacking focus when behind late
bad: Same tactic for 90 minutes whatever the score
Pushing the line to 95 with slow centre-backs while protecting a lead
signals: Score clock: behind after about 70 minutes, and the radar shows your deepest defender still within about 30 m of your own goal.
Score clock: ahead after about 80 minutes with both of your full-backs in the opponent's half.
playbook.fix: Save a lead tactic and a chasing tactic, and switch with D-pad Left when the score and the clock call for it.

sources.title: Best EA FC 27 custom tactics from pro players (Red Bull)

playbook.title: Pick roles that fit the shape you want
playbook.principle: Player roles decide where your AI players go. If both full-backs are attacking wingbacks and both central midfielders are box-to-box, nobody stays back. Pair each attacking role with a holding or defend-focus role.
playbook.why: In FC IQ a Role sets positioning and off-ball decisions and a Focus tilts it. Pro setups pair a Holding midfielder with Box-to-Box players and keep full-backs on Fullback; FUT.GG reports about seven in ten pros use the Defend focus for 4-4-1-1 full-backs.
good: A Holding midfielder next to a Box-to-Box or Deep-Lying Playmaker
One attacking full-back and one defend-focus full-back
bad: Two Attacking Wingbacks with no holding midfielder
Every central player on an attacking focus
signals: Radar, as you lose the ball: both full-backs and both central midfielders are ahead of the ball.
Radar in possession: nobody of yours between your centre-backs and the ball, about 15 to 25 m ahead of them.
playbook.fix: Give every attacking role a partner on the same side with a holding or defend focus.

playbook.title: Substitute tired pressers in time
playbook.principle: Pressing, sprinting and a very high line drain stamina. Tired players recover slowly and lose duels. Plan changes for wide players and pressing midfielders around 60 to 70 minutes, earlier if their indicator has faded.
playbook.why: The Aggressive defensive approach costs extra stamina (FIFA Ultimate Team guide). Player Indicator Fade, on by default, dims the indicator as stamina drops (EA Accessibility), and the Player Name Bar shows a stamina bar. The 60 to 70 minute window is a coaching rule of thumb, not EA data.
good: Planned changes for pressing players before 70 minutes
Checking the name-bar stamina before set pieces late on
bad: Keeping an exhausted full-back on against a fresh winger
Saving all substitutions for injuries
signals: The indicator above a pressing player has faded, or their name-bar stamina is low.
Radar: one of your markers trails the rest of the back line by 5 m or more on recovery runs late in the match.
playbook.fix: Around 60 to 70 minutes, replace the wide players and midfielders whose stamina bars are lowest.

sources.title: FC 27 Player Name Bar (FIFA Ultimate Team guide)

playbook.title: Use skill moves in space, not into a crowd
playbook.principle: Skill moves work when one defender faces you and the next cover is far away. Into a compact block they mostly lose the ball. In FC 27, simple moves such as a ball roll, a drag back or a lane change are often enough against a defender who lunges.
playbook.why: Guides note that simple direction changes beat users now that AI teammates do not auto-tackle, while many users jockey well, so a skill into a set defender rarely works. Moves are limited by the player's Skill Moves stars, and tiers differ between guides.
good: A ball roll or lane change when one defender commits
Passing when two defenders close in
bad: Chaining skills into three defenders
Using a 5-star move when a simple touch would do
signals: Radar: your dribbler has one opponent within about 3 m and the next nearest is more than about 10 m away: a good moment for a move.
Radar: two or more opponents within about 5 m of your dribbler: pass instead.
playbook.fix: Try a skill move only when one defender faces you and the next one is at least ten metres away.

sources.title: FC 27 Skill Moves: all 109 moves by star rating (Keymap)
Pitch Notes: FC 27 Gameplay Deep Dive (EA)

playbook.title: Rush the keeper only when the ball runs loose
playbook.principle: Bringing your keeper out, by holding Triangle or Y, works when a clean-through attacker takes a heavy touch or the ball runs ahead of them. If they have it close and are still outside the box, stay big on the line. A Sweeper Keeper role helps behind a high line.
playbook.why: Sweeper Keeper comes off the line to clear balls behind a high line, and the Rush Out PlayStyle speeds a keeper leaving their goal (FUT.GG, EA). A rush against a close-control attacker invites a chip or a round-the-keeper finish.
good: Rushing when the ball runs several metres ahead of the attacker
Holding the line when the attacker has close control
bad: Rushing early against a striker with the ball at their feet
Leaving the keeper on the line when the ball is rolling free in the box
signals: Radar: an attacker is through with no defender within about 5 m and the ball several metres ahead of them: rush.
Radar: the attacker is still outside your box with the ball close and a defender within about 3 m: stay.
playbook.fix: Rush the keeper only when the ball runs ahead of a clean-through attacker; otherwise hold the line.

sources.title: GK Roles and Focus, EA FC 27 (FUT.GG)
PlayStyles: everything you need to know (EA)

playbook.title: Counter-press for a few seconds, then drop
playbook.principle: After losing the ball high up, the two nearest players should press at once for a few seconds while the rest cover. If the ball escapes, stop pressing and get back into shape. A long chase pulls players out of position.
playbook.why: Coaches' Voice says counter-pressing relies on immediacy and on players already being close together when the ball is lost. A JSSM study found quick regains are the top success factor in defensive transition. In FC 27, Team Press does nothing once the ball reaches your own third.
good: The nearest two players closing the ball within two seconds
Dropping back as soon as the ball passes your midfield
bad: One player chasing alone
Your midfield still chasing in their half after the ball has gone past
signals: Radar, after losing the ball in their half: none of your markers gets within about 5 m of the ball within two seconds.
Radar: your markers still chasing in their half while the ball has passed your midfield line.
playbook.fix: When you lose it high, press with the nearest two players at once and drop back as soon as the ball gets past them.

sources.title: Success factors in defensive transition / rest defence (Journal of Sports Science and Medicine)
How StatsBomb data helps measure counter-pressing (StatsBomb)

playbook.title: Delay when they break with more players
playbook.principle: If they counter three against two, do not dive in. Jockey, back off toward your box and block the pass to the free runner. Every second you delay lets your midfielders get back. Use a professional foul only as a last resort, outside the box.
playbook.why: FIFPlay's FC 27 defending tips advise delaying a counter so teammates can recover. FC 27 jockeying is faster than in FC 26 and manual standing tackles reach further, but a missed tackle leaves a large gap behind (games.gg).
good: Jockeying backwards while showing the attacker toward the touchline
Standing in the passing lane to the free runner
bad: Lunging at the ball carrier with two attackers free beside them
Sliding in from behind outside the box
signals: Radar: three opponents ahead of the ball against two of your markers near your box.
Goal replay: your defender lunged while two attackers were free beside them.
playbook.fix: When they break three against two, jockey backwards and block the pass to the free man until help arrives.

sources.title: Pitch Notes: FC 27 Gameplay Deep Dive (EA)

playbook.title: Match their numbers on the flank
playbook.principle: When two attackers go at your full-back, they cannot win alone. Bring your wide midfielder or a central midfielder back to make it two against two, and show the ball carrier outside. Do not pull a centre-back wide to help.
playbook.why: Overlaps and underlaps create two against one on the flank. FC 27 AI teammates hold shape rather than tracking aggressively, so the user often has to switch to the wide midfielder and run them back. Pulling a centre-back wide opens the middle (see the dont-break-the-line entry).
good: Wide midfielder tracking the overlapping full-back
Full-back showing the winger down the line
bad: Full-back left against two
A centre-back dragged out to the touchline
signals: Radar: two opponent markers against one of yours on a flank in your half, with your nearest midfielder more than about 15 m away.
Goal replay: a cross from a flank where your full-back faced two players.
playbook.fix: When two attackers face your full-back, switch to your nearest wide midfielder and run them back to make it two against two.

sources.title: Glossary: football tactics and coaching definitions (Coaches' Voice)

playbook.title: Check the radar before you receive
playbook.principle: Glance at the radar just before the ball reaches your player. Look for a teammate alone on the far side or a runner behind the press. Many turnovers under pressure happen while a free teammate is off camera.
playbook.why: The camera shows only part of the pitch; the radar shows every player. An FC 25 guide calls the radar the easiest way to find the teammate the opponent has forgotten when pressed, and an EA forum user calls it essential even in co-op.
good: Knowing the free option before the first touch
Playing a switch to a free teammate seen on the radar
bad: Receiving with your eyes only on the ball
Forcing a pass into the pressure side
signals: Radar: when you lost the ball under pressure, one of your markers stood on the far side with no opponent within about 10 m.
Stats screen: low pass accuracy with most losses in the middle third.
playbook.fix: As the pass comes to you, glance at the radar for the free teammate before your first touch.
playbook.drill: Kick-Off vs CPU: before each first touch for ten minutes, say aloud where the free teammate is on the radar.

sources.title: FC 25: how to break pressure and pass successfully, incl. using the radar (IGGM)
Migliore visuale: radar reply (EA Forums, FC 26, Italian)

playbook.title: Make one change at half-time from the stats
playbook.principle: At half-time, read three things: shots and expected goals for each side, possession, and where you lose the ball. Then change one thing only: line height, build-up style, a role focus or a player. Several changes at once hide what worked.
playbook.why: Match Facts show possession, shots, expected goals, passes, tackles and interceptions, with heat maps of where possession was won and lost (FIFA Ultimate Team guide). One change at a time lets the next half tell you whether it helped.
good: Dropping the line five points after two chances conceded in behind
Switching build-up to Short Passing after many long-ball turnovers
bad: Changing formation, roles and line height together
Changing nothing despite a clear pattern
signals: Half-time stats: the opponent's expected goals are higher than yours from fewer shots, a sign of big chances conceded.
Possession heat map: most of your losses come in your own half.
playbook.fix: At half-time, pick the one problem the stats show most clearly and change one setting for it.

sources.title: FC 27 Stats: Match Facts and Performance (FIFA Ultimate Team guide)

playbook.title: Reset after a bad goal or a loss
playbook.principle: After conceding a sloppy goal or losing a match, take a breath before the next action or game. Frustrated players rush passes, foul more and shoot from poor positions. Set a stop rule, such as three losses in a row, and keep it.
playbook.why: Pro guides to Champions weekends advise spreading matches out and reviewing losses rather than playing on while frustrated. The stop rule is a coaching rule of thumb.
good: A short pause and one deep breath after conceding
Stopping after three straight losses
bad: Queuing the next match straight after a frustrating loss
Trying a long shot straight after conceding
signals: Stats screen: pass accuracy and shots on target both drop sharply in the half after you concede.
Several fouls or cards in the minutes after a goal against.
Results: three or more losses in a row.
playbook.fix: After three losses in a row, stop for at least fifteen minutes and review one replay before you play again.

items.name: Release and platforms
items.detail: EA SPORTS FC 27 launched worldwide 25 Sep 2026 (early access before that) on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, PC (EA app/Steam/Epic), Nintendo Switch 2 and last-gen/Switch versions. The Grounds and Clubs are current-gen/PC/Switch 2 only.

items.name: Version as of 2026-10-28
items.detail: Latest is Title Update 1.1.0, released 27 Oct 2026 (the console build may show as 1.07). It has no gameplay balance or tuning changes. Gameplay tuning is otherwise the launch build plus TU 1.0.1 slider tweaks and Live Update #1.

items.name: Two gameplay types: Competitive vs Authentic
items.detail: Competitive gameplay is used in online modes such as Ultimate Team and Rivals. It is tuned for direct user control and has the AI-defending nerf. Authentic Gameplay 2.0 is for Career and Kick-Off: more realistic movement and physicality, varied CPU styles, plus 25 new gameplay sliders and 10 CPU sliders split into Opponent and Teammate.

items.name: Headline gameplay change: AI defending reduced
items.detail: AI teammates no longer stick a leg out to auto-tackle when near the ball carrier. They hold shape and can still pick up loose balls, but the user must time tackles and switch manually. To compensate, jockey speed and manual standing-tackle reach are higher than in FC 26. EA says this applies to Competitive gameplay.

items.name: Headline: more manual passing
items.detail: Through balls follow your aim more strictly, with less correction toward an open lane. Dinked passes are fully manual and are now only on double-tap Through Pass. Crosses drop into the space you aim at instead of homing onto a player, so aim and power decide quality.

items.name: Headline: attacking spatial awareness and curved runs
items.detail: AI attackers weigh space, defensive shape and the offside line, for example holding level with the last defender and then curving in. New inputs are the Triggered Curved Run (tap L1+R1/LB+RB) and Pass & Follow (L1+R1+X/LB+RB+A). Manual runs now stop after a limited distance, and you can retrigger them.

items.name: Headline: manual corners
items.detail: Corners are a three-step sequence: aim and deliver, position players using Avoidance (hold R1/RB) and Shielding (hold L2/LT), then time the header. Attackers no longer auto-move to the best spot. Free kicks and corners have pre-set tactics on D-pad Up.

items.name: Headline: PlayStyles narrowed toward attributes
items.detail: Ten PlayStyles were reworked: Finesse Shot, Technical, Intercept, Rapid, Quick Step, Pinged Pass, Tiki Taka, Jockey, Precision Header and Low Driven. Base attributes matter more. The maximum PlayStyles+ per item fell from 5 to 3. Per a Red Bull pro, a PlayStyle is now worth roughly a 5-10% bonus.

items.name: Patch history: TU 1.0.1 (around 22-23 Sep 2026)
items.detail: Day-zero update with 8 bug fixes and 2 tuning changes. It raised the default Jockey and Sprint Jockey speeds in Authentic gameplay only (Career, Kick-Off), with no effect on Competitive. It also reportedly increased long-term fatigue in Grounds 11v11 (single source). EA kept launch tuning in place to let players adapt.

items.name: Patch history: TU 1.0.2 (28 Sep) and 1.0.3 (2 Oct)
items.detail: No gameplay changes. 1.0.2 fixed the FC Pro Open registration country list. 1.0.3 fixed a Moments loading screen, Grounds matchmaking, duplicates in Club Transfers, and Squad Battles match settings changing unintentionally.

items.name: Patch history: TU 1.0.4 (around 7 Oct 2026)
items.detail: Bug fixes only, with no gameplay tuning. Career fixes: fewer high-OVR/potential generated players, offers get responses instead of instant acceptance, free agents signable with the window closed. Also a FUT post-match error, PS5 player-indicator colours, and FC Lite Kick-Off roster pulls. Dribbling was NOT nerfed.

items.name: Patch history: Live Update #1 (14-15 Oct 2026)
items.detail: Server-side fix with no download (restart the game). It closed the deep free-kick exploit used in Rivals and Champions before Champions Finals. EA acknowledged the exploit on 13 Oct. A separate report of a goalkeeper scoring from free kicks in their own box surfaced around 13 Oct; its fix status is unclear. [Unverified]

items.name: Patch history: TU 1.1.0 (27 Oct 2026)
items.detail: No balance or tuning changes. Fixes: in 1v1 the GK holding the ball after a pass request; in 1v1 the GK taking a free kick instead of the user; 2v2 players stuck in the net after a slide; custom tactics saving wrongly or moving players to wrong positions; 50+ Grounds fixes. Also a redesigned Career Team Management screen, faster high-OVR pack reveals, and persistent SBC filters.

items.name: EA stance on balance (launch feedback update)
items.detail: EA says it will be very measured with core gameplay changes. It is monitoring manual defending (it sees a learning curve: players who adapt win more) and shooting variety, especially near-post low driven shots, which it says can outperform other options. It is broadly happy with the shooting vs GK balance. No nerf as of 28 Oct.

items.name: Closed beta changes that shipped
items.detail: From EA's closed beta feedback update: repeated presses of Shoulder Challenge now make the defender stick an arm out and lose speed (anti-spam), and Team Press has no effect while the ball is in your own defensive third.

items.name: FUT season calendar
items.detail: Season 1 (Ones to Watch theme) ran to Thu 22 Oct 2026. Season 2 runs about 22 Oct to 3 Dec 2026 and is reportedly themed 'FC Heritage', with up to 16 Heritage items on the Standard and Premium ladders. Expected Season 2 promos: Ultimate Scream, UEFA Road to the Knockouts, Hall of FUT Unleashed, Black Friday Thunderstruck. Exact dates are not confirmed by EA. [Unverified]

items.name: Weekly reset times (approximate)
items.detail: Rivals rewards: Thursday 06:59 UTC (per EA help). Squad Battles rewards: Sunday about 06:59 UTC (community-tracked). SP daily cap resets at 07:00 UTC. Champions Finals run Friday evening to Monday morning (UK about 19:00 Fri to 08:00 Mon). Check the in-game timers; the UK moved to GMT on 25 Oct.

items.name: FC Pro 27 esports calendar
items.detail: Open Ladder ran 21 Sep to 3 Oct 2026 in Ultimate Team (Division 5+ in Rivals to enter). Regional qualifiers 10-11 Oct (Battlefy). Global Qualifier LAN in London 5-7 Nov (64 players). FC Pro Open 30 Nov 2026 to 25 Jan 2027 (24 players, groups then finals; top 8 to Worlds). $1M World Championship; over $2.5M season pool. Worlds date TBC.

items.name: FC 27 Lite (free version)
items.detail: A free limited client with Kick-Off, Learn to Play, Online Friendlies and Online Seasons. No Ultimate Team, Manager Career or The Grounds. EA lists it on PlayStation, Xbox, EA app, Steam and Epic. Progress carries over to the full game on the same EA account and platform.

items.name: Critical reception
items.detail: Reviews call FC 27 an evolution. Game Informer gave it 7.25/10. Praise goes to the Career overhaul (TransferRoom transfers, Dynamic OVR) and the more manual defending and passing. Criticism: The Grounds feels unfinished, AI teammate decisions are poor, and some EA forum users feel running, passing and shooting took a step back.

items.name: What a screen-only coach can measure
items.detail: The visible score clock, radar dots, player indicators, power bars, the pause-menu Match Facts (possession, shots, xG, passes, tackles), half-time and full-time summaries, Rivals and Champions progress screens, and tactics screens. Never read memory. Infer the opponent's shape from radar dot spacing and the line from the defender dots.

items.name: Scope note on verification
items.detail: Much FC 27 detail comes from third-party guides (FUT.GG, FIFPlay, NealGuides, timesaver.gg, Dexerto and others) because ea.com could not be fetched directly. Items marked [Unverified] conflict between sources or rest on a single source. Exact button inputs and reward numbers should be confirmed in-game.

items.name: Game identity
items.detail: EA SPORTS FC 27, the fourth EA SPORTS FC title, published by Electronic Arts. Worldwide release Friday 25 Sep 2026; Ultimate Edition early access from 18 Sep; Web App 16 Sep and Companion App 17 Sep; 10-hour EA Play trial. Platforms as in the existing pack (PS5, Xbox Series X|S, PC, Switch 2 and others).

items.name: TU 1.1.0 timing and scope
items.detail: Latest download is Title Update 1.1.0, live 27 Oct 2026 (about 11:16 CET per one guide), described as 150-plus fixes and quality-of-life changes with no balance or tuning changes. Gameplay tuning is the launch build plus TU 1.0.1's Authentic-only jockey change and Live Update #1 (free-kick exploit fix, 14-15 Oct).

items.name: EA's stated patch stance
items.detail: In its closed-beta update EA said that, unlike previous FC titles, it does not plan significant gameplay balance changes in early title updates. Its 30 Sep and 13 Oct updates repeat that an item on the watch list does not mean a change is coming.

items.name: EA watch list (13 Oct 2026)
items.detail: Full-backs dropping too deep and keeping attackers onside; kick-off goals; near-post low driven shots; interceptions by players with low defensive attributes; foul calls after some challenges. Manual defending: data shows a learning curve, no change planned.

items.name: 9 Oct fix
items.detail: A server-side fix on 9 Oct tuned FUT Champions matchmaking after the first Finals weekend. It was not a defending change, despite some reports.

items.name: Closed-beta changes: full list
items.detail: Lower depth settings retreat earlier; Team Press off in your defensive third and weaker from defenders; shoulder-challenge spam slows the defender; challenges from behind less reliable; Bruiser+ slightly reduced; triggered runs capped; Player Lock carrier no longer dribbles by itself; dinked pass removed from the Ground Pass input.

items.name: What changes the screen
items.detail: Radar 2D/3D/Off and its colours, Score Clock and Dropdown toggles, Player Indicator size/fade/colours (custom per player in FC 27), Player Name Bar, HyperMotion Insight Overlays, Scrolling Line Ups, High Contrast Gameplay and colour-blind filters. Any of these can break vision assumptions.

items.name: Ultimate Team (FUT) overview
items.detail: Build a squad from player items via packs, SBCs, Evolutions, objectives and the Transfer Market, then play online (Rivals, Champions, Live Events, Rush, Friendlies) or offline (Squad Battles, single-player Live Events, Moments). It uses Competitive gameplay. The Competitive settings preset is the FUT default.

items.name: Division Rivals: structure
items.detail: 10 numbered divisions (10 lowest) plus Elite. Weekly points: win 3, draw 1, loss 0. Base weekly reward at 15-29 points, Upgrade at 30+. Extra points help climbing divisions only. Win streaks speed up stage progress. Elite uses a Skill Rating that starts at 500 instead of stages.

items.name: Division Rivals: rewards
items.detail: Weekly rewards scale by division and are claimed Thursday 06:59 UTC. Launch-update pack rewards are tradeable. CQP by division per week (one source): Elite 1000, Div 1 750, Div 2 600, Div 3 500, Div 4 400 ... Div 10 50. Coin figures conflict between sites. Rivals wins pay about 70 SP. Bounties appear more often.

items.name: Division Rivals: matchmaking note
items.detail: Matchmaking blends division and skill. Community reports that Division 6-ish lobbies can feel harder than Champions because of skill-based matching. Pros advise not to judge progress on single results. [Unverified]

items.name: FUT Champions: qualification
items.detail: Earn 1,000 Champions Qualification Points (CQP) for Season 1. CQP comes from Division Rivals weekly rewards and a Squad Battles World Class wins objective. There is no division requirement (the old Division 6 gate was removed); a higher division just earns CQP faster. Every Finals finish refunds some CQP, e.g. 8 wins gives 400.

items.name: FUT Champions: Finals format
items.detail: Up to 15 matches over a weekend window (Friday evening to Monday morning UK). Each win moves you up one rank; losses do not cost rank. 15 ranks: Contender (1-5 wins), Champions (6-10), Elite (11-15). The FC 26 Play-Offs stage and Challengers mode were removed.

items.name: Squad Battles
items.detail: Offline vs AI squads (user-created plus featured TOTW and promo squads). Battle Points depend on difficulty (about 0.5x Beginner to 2.6x Ultimate for a win), opponent rating and chem, result, and goals (capped at 5). Weekly match cap: sources say 14 or 18 counted games. Quitting early gives 0 points. Win about 50 SP. Rewards on Sunday by rank, Elite 1 to Top 200. [Unverified]

items.name: Squad Battles CQP objective
items.detail: A seasonal objective awards Champions Qualification Points for wins on World Class difficulty, with milestones reported at 10, 12 and 15 wins. It lets offline players help qualify for Champions.

items.name: Rush (Ultimate Team)
items.detail: Small-sided mode with 4 user outfield players plus an AI GK (5v5 in FUT; FC 25-26 format carried over, not explicitly confirmed by EA). Weekly Rush Points tiers run from 2,500 to 35,000 points and are earned by playing, winning and completing Block challenges in squad building. Weekly Rush rewards are untradeable. [Unverified]

items.name: Rush rules (series convention)
items.detail: Rush rules in FC 25-26: short matches on a compact pitch, kick-off by racing to a ball from your own goal line, offside only in the final third, blue card (temporary sin bin), and a penalty from a shot run-up. FC 27 has a Rush tutorial covering offsides, corners, penalties and Blue Cards. Specifics are not confirmed for FC 27. [Unverified]

items.name: Live Events (FUT)
items.detail: Rotating themed competitions, both multiplayer and single-player vs AI, with entry rules (e.g. league or rarity limits) and objective-linked rewards. A win is worth about 60 SP.

items.name: Moments (FUT)
items.detail: Short single-player scenarios with set objectives (score X, assist, etc.). They earn Stars, which are exchanged in the Moments Gallery. TU 1.0.3 fixed a Moments challenge loading-screen hang.

items.name: FUT Friendlies
items.detail: Casual matches (Play a Friend, Couch Play, themed friendlies) with no effect on ranking. Good for testing tactics and settings without pressure.

items.name: Squad Building Challenges (SBC) - FC 27 changes
items.detail: Streamlined SBCs give each item a number that adds toward the goal, instead of requiring up to 11 specific players. Some streamlined SBCs drop rating, chem and position requirements. TU 1.1.0 keeps saved SBC filters within a session.

items.name: Evolutions - FC 27 changes
items.detail: Evolutions now use branching Pathways: pick between upgrade routes and preview the chain before committing. They upgrade stats, PlayStyles, roles and cosmetics after completing match objectives.

items.name: FUT Gallery and Holographics
items.detail: The Gallery permanently records every player you have owned, even if discarded or used in an SBC. Themed sets are graded D to S, raise your Gallery Level and unlock tokens, cosmetics and Holographic items. Holographics are rarer animated variants (Regular and Pristine) with identical stats that count more toward sets. Gallery cards are not consumed.

items.name: Hall of FUT
items.detail: A new tier of players tied to Ultimate Team memories (launch class includes Akinfenwa, Loic Remy, Eljero Elia). Base items are only obtainable from the Gallery Token Store. Special versions arrive via campaigns. Chemistry works like Heroes.

items.name: FUT chemistry changes
items.detail: ICONs keep full chem in position and +1 to every league, but their nation contribution drops from +2 to +1. Heroes (and Hall of FUT) keep a +1 nation link, but their league contribution drops from +2 to +1. Base ICONs start at 88 OVR.

items.name: Season Pass and SP
items.detail: Season Pass levels are earned with SP. Match SP ranges from 15 to 100 per eligible match by mode and result, with an 850 SP daily cap from matches (reset 07:00 UTC). Objectives add more: dailies about 30, weeklies about 500, seasonal about 500 per week. Grounds and Career also feed the pass. Pass progress resets at season end.

items.name: Manager Career
items.detail: Rebuilt transfers with TransferRoom integration and Expected Transfer Value (xTV) pricing. Staged negotiations with buy-back, sell-on and loan-back clauses, instalments and bonuses. Dynamic OVR (form, morale, fitness). Coaches forecast potential. Practice Arena replaces Training Plans. Also Manager Live, Creator Challenges, Liga MX, ICONs, and simulation for up to 10 leagues.

items.name: Career: Dynamic OVR
items.detail: A player's current OVR moves with Form, Morale and Match Fitness without changing base ability. Morale is driven by playing time, squad role, expectations and interactions. It is shown in Team Management, Squad Hub, Development Plans and Scout Reports. Out-of-position penalties vary by versatility.

items.name: Career: Practice Arena
items.detail: In the Career Central hub you can play 11v11 practice matches of your starting XI vs reserves. They inherit your gameplay type and sliders, so they are a good sandbox to rehearse tactics.

items.name: Career: Creator Challenges and Manager Live
items.detail: Creator Challenges are custom scenarios (narrative, rules, win conditions) built and shared through a web dashboard. Manager Live is a set of live, rotating manager challenges. Exact reward structures are not covered here. [Unverified]

items.name: Career: TU 1.1.0 additions
items.detail: Redesigned Team Management screen, per-save toggle for Press Conferences, adjustable frequency of Unexpected Events, new rivalry objectives (Consistency Rivalries, Match Limit Rivalries), and negotiation rejections that now explain why.

items.name: Player Career
items.detail: Play as one footballer. New in FC 27: Rivalries against AI players in your role, plus Liga MX and ICONs. CPU Teammate and CPU Opponent sliders are separate in Authentic Gameplay 2.0, which helps single-player control.

items.name: The Grounds (new social hub)
items.detail: Open-world hub for your created Pro with up to 100 players across three districts: Parkside (UK), Montclair (French cage football) and Zeiza (Argentine potrero), linked by the Terrace. Pitches host 1v1, 2v2, 3v3 and Rush, plus minigames (Balloon Ball, Bucket Ball, Goal Control, Big Race, Attacking Scenarios, Bocce Ball). Current-gen/PC/Switch 2 only.

items.name: The Grounds progression
items.detail: Archetype XP (AXP), Grounds Coins, Masteries and Amps. All 13 Archetypes are unlocked from the start, and resets are free. Masteries give permanent attribute boosts per Archetype. Amps are temporary modifiers (2 Standard plus 1 Signature that adds PlayStyles or perks) that expire after N matches. Grounds also feeds the Season Pass.

items.name: Clubs (inside The Grounds)
items.detail: Clubs now lives inside The Grounds: walk to the Clubhouse entrance for Leagues (points-based promotion and relegation) and Playoffs, or to Stadium Access for 11v11 Drop-In and Rush. New Club Tournaments are 11v11 with House Rules variants. EA says bigger Grounds and Clubs features are coming in a future update.

items.name: Clubs Archetypes (13)
items.detail: Shot Stopper, Sweeper Keeper, Progressor, Boss, Marauder, Disruptor, Recycler, Maestro, Creator, Spark, Magician, Finisher, Target. Each Mastery raises two attributes (e.g. Finisher: Composure and Finishing). Sources disagree on some positional groupings.

items.name: Kick-Off
items.detail: Local matches vs CPU or couch co-op using Authentic gameplay. Match types: Classic, House Rules, Rush (sources say 3v3 or 5v5), Best Of series, Cup finals and licensed competition matches. A good place to drill the new corners and runs. [Unverified]

items.name: Online Seasons and Co-Op Seasons
items.detail: Ranked 1v1 with real clubs or national teams: 10-game seasons to earn promotion and titles through divisions. Co-Op Seasons is the 2v2 version with a friend against other duos. Uses Competitive-style online settings.

items.name: Online Friendlies
items.detail: Matches against an invited friend with real teams. Sources describe it either as one-offs or as a five-match mini-season. [Unverified]

items.name: Learn to Play / Training
items.detail: Skill Games and the training arena for drilling new mechanics such as low driven double-tap timing, curved runs, Avoidance and Shielding on corners, and jockey/tackle timing. Included in FC Lite.

items.name: FC Pro Open Ladder entry
items.detail: Esports qualification runs through Ultimate Team. Reach Division 5 or above in Division Rivals to become eligible for the in-game FC Pro Open Ladder (FC 27 window was 21 Sep to 3 Oct 2026).

items.name: Ultimate Team Draft
items.detail: Entry 15,000 coins, 300 FC Points or a Draft Token. Pick a squad from five formation options, then play up to four matches until you lose. Online Draft vs people; Single Player Draft vs CPU-controlled real clubs (difficulty changes coins per match only). Rewards at the end; reward tables are community-tracked.

items.name: Rush (FC 27)
items.detail: 5v5 available in Ultimate Team, Clubs, Kick-Off and Career. FUT Rush uses AI keepers. Pitch 63.7 x 46.6 m. Four Quick Chat categories with four messages each.
