Leaving early: matchmaking penalties of 15 minutes to 1 hour, removed by completing matches. Blue cards and run-up penalties were FC 25 rules; FC 27 carry-over not confirmed.

items.name: Kick-Off match types
items.detail: Classic Match, Rush, House Rules, licensed competition matches, Cup Finals, Home & Away and Best Of series. House Rules include Survival, Mystery Ball, Headers & Volleys and No Rules; Long Range and King of the Hill appear in events and Club Tournaments.

items.name: House Rules details
items.detail: Survival: after each goal a random outfield player of the scoring team is removed. Mystery Ball: when the ball goes out it can return as one of five Mystery Ball types with temporary boosts. Normal positional coaching may not apply in these.

items.name: Clubs competitions in FC 27
items.detail: Reached through the Clubhouse. Leagues: points from wins and draws, promotion and relegation, divisions reset each season, then Playoffs. Club Tournaments: 11v11 with varied rounds, rewards and House Rules (King of the Hill, Survival, Long Range, No Rules). Live Tournaments rotate rules. Stadium Drop-In is matchmade 11v11. Rush Stadium and an in-world Rush pitch.

items.name: The Grounds activities
items.detail: 1v1 to 4v4 pitches, Rush small-sided, Kickabouts and minigames across Parkside, Montclair and Zeiza around the Terrace, up to 100 players. Small-sided matches leave the open world for matchmaking.

items.name: Manager Career additions
items.detail: Tactical Visions set a baseline playstyle template; coaches hired per position group boost that system. Practice Arena runs 11v11 starting XI vs reserves using your sliders, the best offline sandbox for this pack's drills.

items.name: FC 27 Lite
items.detail: Free client: Kick-Off, Learn to Play, Online Friendlies, Online Seasons; no Ultimate Team, Manager Career or The Grounds.

items.name: Defensive third
items.detail: The third nearest your goal. Team Press has NO effect while the ball is here (FC 27 change). Defend with manual jockey and switching here; do not pull CBs out to press.

items.name: Middle third
items.detail: Most pressing and turnovers happen here. Team Press and an Aggressive/95 line are most effective here; Second Man Press/Teammate Contain help close passing lanes.

items.name: Final third
items.detail: Where through balls, curved runs and cut-backs decide chances. Against a high line, the space is BEHIND the defence rather than between the lines.

items.name: Space behind a high line
items.detail: When the opponent's line height is 90+ (Aggressive, default 95), lofted or lobbed through balls into this channel, timed before your striker drifts offside, are the primary counter.

items.name: Half-spaces
items.detail: Channels between the touchline lanes and the centre. Inside Forwards and Shadow Strikers exploit them; curved runs from here bend around CBs.

items.name: Zone 14 / edge of the box
items.detail: Central area just outside the box. Home to the CAM, Shadow Striker and Playmaker. Finesse and low driven shots are taken from here; the 4-3-1-2 and 4-2-1-3 overload it.

items.name: Wide channels / flanks
items.detail: The weakness of narrow formations (4-3-1-2, 4-1-2-1-2): fullbacks are isolated. Switch play here when the opponent commits players to one side.

items.name: Near-post zone
items.detail: Near-post low driven shots are acknowledged by EA as strong in FC 27. As an attacker aim near post when the GK gives an opening; as a defender cover the near post in 1v1s.

items.name: Penalty box and six-yard box
items.detail: Low driven shots are recommended inside the box and in 1v1s. On corners, positioning (Avoidance/Shielding) inside the six-yard and penalty-spot areas decides headers.

items.name: Corner positioning spots
items.detail: Near post, far post, penalty spot, edge of the box. In FC 27 attackers do not auto-move to the best spot. Use Avoidance (hold R1/RB) to slip through and Shielding (hold L2/LT) to hold position, then time the header.

items.name: Grounds: Parkside
items.detail: UK-inspired district of The Grounds hub with its own pitches, stores and activities.

items.name: Grounds: Montclair
items.detail: French-inspired district built around cage football.

items.name: Grounds: Zeiza
items.detail: Argentine potrero-inspired district.

items.name: Grounds: The Terrace
items.detail: Central area connecting the three districts. The Clubhouse entrance (Leagues, Playoffs) and Stadium Access (11v11 Drop-In, Rush) are reachable from the hub.

items.name: Main menu / Football Club hub
items.detail: The home screen has tiles for Ultimate Team, Career, The Grounds/Clubs, Kick-Off, Online and Settings. Settings > Game Settings, then R1/RB to reach Visual Settings (radar, indicators). FC 27 layout specifics are not verified. [Unverified]

items.name: Pause menu
items.detail: Pausing during a match opens Resume, Match Facts/Performance (stats), Team Management/Tactics (subs, formation, roles), Settings, and Quit/Forfeit. Online pauses are limited and timed. Recognise it by the dimmed pitch behind a vertical menu list. [Unverified]

items.name: Match Facts screen (how to recognise)
items.detail: Opened from pause, half-time or full-time. It shows a two-column team comparison: Possession %, Shots, Shots on Target, xG (expected goals), Passes, Pass Accuracy, Tackles (won), Interceptions, Fouls, Corners, Offsides, Yellow/Red cards. L1/R1 or LB/RB cycles between stat groups. [Unverified]

items.name: Performance / heat map tabs
items.detail: Further tabs show possession heat maps (overall, won, lost), shot maps (all shots, goals, off target, blocked, saved), player ratings, distance covered and minutes played. Use them to diagnose where the ball is lost and which shot zones fail. [Unverified]

items.name: HyperMotion Insight Overlays
items.detail: An optional setting that displays live stat overlays (e.g. possession, shot or xG pop-ups, player sprint stats) during play without pausing. When it is enabled the coach may see transient stat banners. [Unverified]

items.name: Half-time screen
items.detail: At 45' a half-time transition shows the score with a stats summary (possession, shots, xG). Online there is a short countdown to make subs and tactics changes. A good moment to show the coach's half-time debrief. [Unverified]

items.name: Full-time / post-match screen
items.detail: Shows the final score, match facts and Player of the Match. In FUT it is followed by the rewards screen (coins, SP, objectives progress) and, for Rivals and Champions, a progress screen (points bar, stage, rank). [Unverified]

items.name: Rivals progress screen
items.detail: After a Rivals match a progress bar shows weekly points (3 win, 1 draw), 15 and 30 point thresholds for Base and Upgrade rewards, stage stars and division. A useful OCR target for tracking the weekly target. [Unverified]

items.name: Champions Finals hub
items.detail: Shows matches played out of 15, wins, current rank (Contender, Champions or Elite tiers) and the time left in the weekend window. [Unverified]

items.name: Replay / instant replay
items.detail: Goals trigger a celebration then highlight replays from several cameras, with a transition wipe (logo swipe) before and after. Radar, score clock and player indicators are typically hidden during replays. Skip with the button prompt. Do not count replay frames as live play. [Unverified]

items.name: Team Management / Tactics screen
items.detail: Formation pitch view with player cards, a Roles and Focus selector per position, and Custom Tactics tabs: Build-Up Style, Defensive Approach plus Line Height slider. Up to 5 saved tactics (shareable codes). A TU 1.1.0 fix addressed tactics saving incorrectly. [Unverified]

items.name: Set-piece overlay
items.detail: On corners and free kicks an aiming arc and indicator appears. D-pad Up opens set-piece tactics (moved from D-pad Down for corners in FC 27). On corners a short positioning window follows delivery.

items.name: Tactics D-pad overlay
items.detail: D-pad Left during play opens My Tactics (5 saved Custom Tactics, switching takes a moment). D-pad Right opens Tactical Focus (Default/Attacking/Defending). A small banner confirms the change.

items.name: Loading / pre-match screen
items.detail: Team line-ups, kit and stadium, followed by the walk-out and kick-off. In FUT the squad rating and chemistry appear on the line-up card. [Unverified]

items.name: Squad Battles results screen
items.detail: Shows Battle Points earned, broken into result, difficulty multiplier, goals and performance, plus weekly rank. [Unverified]

items.name: Score clock (scoreboard)
items.detail: Normally top-left: team short names or crests, score, match clock in minutes, and an added-time (+X) badge late in each half. It can be hidden in accessibility/visual settings. Use OCR here to read the score and minute. [Unverified]

items.name: Radar (mini-map)
items.detail: Bottom-centre pitch overview in 2D (top-down) or 3D, or off. Dots show both teams and the ball, with configurable dot colours (team colours recommended). Pros favour 2D. Read the opponent's line height and shape from the dot positions. [Unverified]

items.name: Player indicator
items.detail: A marker above the controlled player (arrow, name or number, or a name bar) with a stamina bar. The size and type are configurable, e.g. Player Name Large. The indicator can fade with stamina loss. A Next Player Switch indicator shows the L1/LB switch target.

items.name: Power bar
items.detail: A bar appears under or near the player for shots, passes, crosses and set pieces, showing charge. It is useful for coaching over-powered shots and passes. [Unverified]

items.name: Set-piece aiming arc
items.detail: On corners and free kicks a trajectory and aim marker shows the delivery target. FC 27 adds a short post-delivery window to move attackers.

items.name: Card and event banners
items.detail: Booking (yellow/red), substitution, injury, offside and goal banners appear as overlays, typically lower-third or near the scoreboard. [Unverified]

items.name: Camera: Tele Broadcast
items.detail: Recommended for competitive play by many guides: Height about 10-20, Zoom about 0-5, Power Shot Zoom off, camera shake off. Gives a higher, wider view of passing lanes.

items.name: Camera: Co-Op
items.detail: Wider horizontal view favoured by some guides for 11v11. It shows runs and shape without relying on the radar as much.

items.name: Broadcast camera / presentation
items.detail: The default broadcast-style camera with TV-style graphics. Not ideal for competitive vision. FC 27-specific broadcast package details were not found. [Unverified]

items.name: Pass Receiver Lock indicator
items.detail: When Pass Receiver Lock is on, control locks onto the intended receiver. Most guides set it to Late, so the lock engages after the kick and you can control the passer longer.

items.name: Radar: Where and what
items.detail: Small top-down pitch map, usually bottom centre, showing all 22 players and the ball. Settings: Game Settings > Visual > Radar (2D / 3D / Off), User Radar Colour, Opponent Radar Colour. Position and size are not adjustable.

items.name: Radar: Default view
items.detail: EA's FIFA 22 settings page names 2D as the default; no FC 26 or FC 27 page states one. Ask the player to confirm 2D.

items.name: Radar: Colour values
items.detail: Default, Red, Blue, Green, Purple, Orange, White, Black for each team. Default follows normal kit colours, ignoring High Contrast kit colours (FC 26 report). Recommend fixed contrasting colours such as Blue for you and Red or Orange for the opponent.

items.name: Radar: Direction
items.detail: Goals sit left and right; teams change ends at half-time, so your attacking direction on the radar flips. Re-detect each half from your keeper's marker.

items.name: Radar: Reading distances
items.detail: Assume 105 x 68 m. 10 m is about a tenth of the radar length; the penalty area is about a sixth. Use 2D; 3D is perspective-distorted.

items.name: Radar: Unverified details
items.detail: How the ball and the controlled player are drawn, which pitch lines are shown, and whether the radar hides at set pieces and replays are not documented. Validate on live captures.

items.name: Radar: Known complaints
items.detail: FC 26 Clubs players report the radar can look too transparent and dark indicator colours blend into the pitch; there is no opacity option.

items.name: Radar: position
items.detail: default: Bottom centre of the screen, below the action, drawn as a small landscape pitch. This is the long-standing FIFA/FC layout seen in footage; no EA page states the position.. movable: No option to move or resize the radar appears in any FC 25, FC 26 or FC 27 settings list found (FIFPlay, FIFA Ultimate Team guide, EA Accessibility pages).

items.name: Radar: shape
items.detail: 2D: a flat rectangle in pitch proportions (a real 105 x 68 m pitch is about 1.54:1), goals at the left and right ends. 3D: the same pitch drawn tilted in perspective, so the far touchline is shorter than the near one and distances are compressed toward the top. Use 2D for any distance measurement. (Unverified.)

items.name: Radar: views
items.detail: 2D: Top-down flat radar. EA's FIFA 22 PC settings page describes '2D or 3D top down viewing angles' and names 2D as the default. Recommended for the coach: positions map linearly to the pitch. 3D: Tilted perspective radar (EA: radar appearance can be set as 2D or 3D depending on preference).

items.name: Radar: views (2)
items.detail: Distances are not linear; the coach should ask the player to switch to 2D or apply a perspective correction. Off: Hides the radar. Listed for FC 25 and FC 26 by FIFPlay and for FC 27 by the FIFA Ultimate Team settings guide. With the radar off, every radar-based signal in this pack fails closed.

items.name: Radar: default
items.detail: 2D is the documented default in FIFA 22 (EA Accessibility). No FC 26 or FC 27 source names the default; assume 2D but check on first run. (Unverified.)

items.name: Radar: menu path
items.detail: allPlatforms: Main menu > Settings (gear icon, top right) > Game Settings > Visual tab > Radar section: Radar (2D / 3D / Off), User Radar Colour, Opponent Radar Colour. The Visual tab also holds the Overlays section (Score Clock, Score Clock Dropdown, HyperMotion Insight Overlays, Scrolling Line Ups) and the indicator options..

items.name: Radar: menu path (2)
items.detail: ps5: Use R1 / L1 to move between the Game Settings tabs to reach Visual.. xbox: Use RB / LB to move between the Game Settings tabs to reach Visual.. pc: Same menus; tab-switch keys on keyboard were not confirmed (controller bumpers work)..

items.name: Radar: menu path (3)
items.detail: inMatch: Pause > Settings > Game Settings > Visual reaches the same options during a match (MagicGameWorld reports the score clock option can be changed from the pause menu).. accessibilityFilter: FC 27 adds an Accessibility filter in the Settings menu that narrows the list to accessibility-relevant options, with icons marking settings that may help (EA FC 27 Accessibility page).

items.name: Radar: colours
items.detail: userRadarColour: Changes the colour of the radar icons for your own team (EA FC 26 Accessibility page wording).. opponentRadarColour: Changes the colour of the radar icons for the opposing team.. values: Default, Red, Blue, Green, Purple, Orange, White, Black.

items.name: Radar: colours (2)
items.detail: valuesSource: Exact list on EA's FIFA 20 and FIFA 22 settings pages and FIFPlay FC 24; the FIFA Ultimate Team FC 27 guide lists the same values as User/Opponent Radar Indicator Colour. EA's FC 26 page shows 'User Radar Colour' set to Default on the Visual Settings screen.. defaultLooksLike: Default follows each team's normal kit colour.

items.name: Radar: colours (3)
items.detail: An FC 26 player using High Contrast Mode reports the radar 'takes the colour of the standard kit, not the high contrast one', and that a team in a dark kit forced them to change the radar colour manually before each match. So with Default, two dark kits (or two white kits) can look alike on the radar..

items.name: Radar: colours (4)
items.detail: highContrastInteraction: High Contrast Mode (FC 26 and FC 27) recolours players, keepers, referee and ball on the pitch, but per the same report the radar ignores those colours. Unconfirmed whether FC 27 fixed this.. recommendation: Ask the player to set fixed, contrasting colours, for example User Radar Colour Blue and Opponent Radar Colour Red or Orange.

items.name: Radar: colours (5)
items.detail: Avoid White and Black for teams (white may be confused with the ball; black and dark colours blend into the radar background, as an FC 26 forum post reports for dark indicator colours), and avoid Green on a green pitch. Record the choice in player context so the coach knows which colour is 'you'.

items.name: Radar: ball
items.detail: Not documented by EA. Expect a small, light (white) marker smaller than the player markers. Confirm on live captures; if the player chooses White for a team the ball may be hard to separate. (Unverified.)

items.name: Radar: controlled player
items.detail: Not documented. Expect the user-controlled player's marker to be highlighted in the player-indicator colour rather than the team colour. FC 27 adds custom per-player indicator colours (Player Indicator Colours: Default or Custom), so the coach must not hard-code the highlight colour. In couch co-op several markers may be highlighted. (Unverified.)

items.name: Radar: numbers and names
items.detail: No source mentions shirt numbers or names on the radar. Treat markers as anonymous: identify roles from position (deepest marker near a goal line is the keeper, and so on). (Unverified.)

items.name: Radar: pitch markings
items.detail: Not documented for FC 27. Expect the pitch outline, halfway line, centre circle and both penalty areas drawn as light lines on a darker, semi-transparent pitch. Calibrate scale from the outline, not from guessed markings. (Unverified.)

items.name: Radar: transparency
items.detail: No transparency or opacity option exists in the FC 25, FC 26 or FC 27 settings lists found. An FC 26 Clubs player reports the mini-map 'can become too transparent', making positions hard to read, and that darker individual indicator colours blend into the pitch; they ask EA for an opacity option. No EA reply or change was found.

items.name: Radar: visibility
items.detail: replays: Expected hidden during goal replays, instant replays and cutscenes, along with the score clock and indicators. Do not read radar positions from replay frames.. setPieces: Expected visible at corners, free kicks and throw-ins; not confirmed. FC 27 corners move the camera to the box for the positioning window (Red Bull), which may change what the HUD shows..

items.name: Radar: visibility (2)
items.detail: penalties: Not confirmed; treat penalty frames as having no radar.. menus: Hidden in pause, half-time and full-time screens.

items.name: Radar: modes
items.detail: Radar is a global Game Setting, so it applies to 11v11 matches in every mode that uses the normal match HUD (Kick-Off, Career, Ultimate Team, Online Seasons, Clubs). Clubs players rely on it heavily (FC 26 forum). Whether Rush (5v5) and The Grounds small-sided pitches show a radar was not confirmed. (Unverified.)

items.name: Radar: orientation
items.detail: The radar shows the pitch the same way round as the main side-on camera: goals at the left and right ends. Teams change ends at half-time (and for the second period of extra time), so your attacking direction on the radar flips each half. No FC setting was found that fixes your team to attack one way in 11v11.

items.name: Radar: orientation (2)
items.detail: Infer direction each half from where your goalkeeper's marker sits, or from which half your team occupies at kick-off. On vertical cameras the radar orientation was not checked. )

items.name: Radar: accessibility
items.detail: User Radar Colour and Opponent Radar Colour (Default plus 7 colours) are the radar's only colour controls. High Contrast Mode / High Contrast Gameplay: colours for home players, home keeper, away players, away keeper, ball and referee, a pitch-saturation slider, and where to apply the colours (Can I Play That? FC 26; returns in FC 27).

items.name: Radar: accessibility (2)
items.detail: The radar reportedly keeps Default kit colours regardless. Colour-blind filters: Protanopia, Deuteranopia, Tritanopia with an intensity slider (one walkthrough: 0-10, default 6). A filter changes every on-screen colour, including radar markers, so calibrate colours after the player turns one on. FC 27: Player Indicator Colours can be Default or Custom (pick a colour per team member).

items.name: Radar: accessibility (3)
items.detail: This changes the controlled-player highlight. Accessibility filter in the FC 27 Settings menu.

items.name: Radar: score clock
items.detail: position: Top-left of the screen: home team short name, home score, away score, away short name, then the match clock in minutes, with an added-time badge late in each half.. options: Visual > Overlays: Score Clock On (default) / Off and Score Clock Dropdown On (default) / Off. When Off, these elements are hidden during gameplay (EA Accessibility FC 26 and FC 27)..

items.name: Radar: score clock (2)
items.detail: dropdown: The Score Clock Dropdown is a panel that drops below the score clock for in-match information (for example events and stat graphics). Its exact contents in FC 27 were not confirmed.. risk: MagicGameWorld reports the Score Clock can end up switched off by default or after an update.

items.name: Radar: score clock (3)
items.detail: If it is off, the score and minute cannot be read: fail closed and ask the player to turn it back on.. styles: Licensed competitions may use their own broadcast-style score bug; FC 27 specifics were not found.

items.name: Radar: reading guide
items.detail: Calibrate once per session: find the radar rectangle near the bottom centre, measure its outline in pixels, and map it to a 105 x 68 m pitch (assumption; FC pitch size is not published). 5 m deep) is about one sixth of it; the radar's height is the pitch width (68 m). Team identity: use the colours the player set (recommended fixed User and Opponent colours).

items.name: Radar: reading guide (2)
items.detail: With Default colours, sample each team's colour at kick-off and re-check after half-time. Direction: at each kick-off note which end your goalkeeper's marker is at; your team attacks the other end until half-time, then reverse. Ignore radar frames during replays, menus, set-piece cut-ins and goal celebrations. Prefer 2D. If the player uses 3D, request 2D or treat distances as approximate.

items.name: Radar: reading guide (3)
items.detail: Markers are anonymous: assign roles by position (keeper, back line, midfield, forwards) using sorted x-positions.

items.name: Radar: known issues
items.detail: Default radar colours ignore High Contrast kit colours (FC 26 report). Radar can look too transparent with dark indicator colours (FC 26 Clubs report). No opacity, size or position option.

items.name: Formation: 4-2-1-3 (launch meta)
items.detail: The most-used FUT formation at launch (about 25% of squads on FUT.GG). Two CDMs give cover now that AI defending is weaker. Typical: CDMs Deep-Lying Playmaker plus Holding, CAM Playmaker or Shadow Striker, Inside Forwards on the wings, ST Advanced Forward, Balanced build-up, line about 60. It needs pace on both wide forwards.

items.name: Formation: 4-3-1-2 (pro favourite)
items.detail: The most-used shape among FC 27 pros per FUTSettings and FUT.GG (about 29-31% of pros). No wingers, so the centre is overloaded: CMs Box-to-Box or Holding, CAM Shadow Striker, two STs Advanced Forward, Fullbacks. Vejrgang: Balanced build-up, Balanced line 60. Weakness: width, as the fullbacks are isolated.

items.name: Formation: 4-4-1-1
items.detail: Popular community pick (about 31% of squads per U7buy) and recommended by Tekkz in Red Bull's guide. Safe against counters with two banks of four, and the second striker links play. Good for counter-attacking.

items.name: Formation: 4-2-3-1 Wide
items.detail: Balanced option for protecting leads, with two CDMs plus wide midfielders for width.

items.name: Formation: 4-1-2-1-2 Narrow
items.detail: Central diamond. Strong through the middle and on combination play, but vulnerable on the flanks.

items.name: Formation: 4-4-2 Flat
items.detail: Beginner-friendly and balanced. Vejrgang's FC 25-26 favourite. Only two CMs, so a lost midfield duel exposes the back line. Skycoach suggests line height about 55.

items.name: Formation: 4-2-2-2
items.detail: Two CDMs plus two CAM/inside players and two strikers. Narrow and compact, central overloads.

items.name: Formation: 4-3-3 / 4-5-1 Flat
items.detail: Wider midfield shapes. The 4-5-1 Flat is often paired with Short Passing build-up and a High line about 70 (FUT.GG).

items.name: Formation: 5-3-2
items.detail: Strongest defensive shape per Skycoach, but rarely used. Back-five cover suits users who struggle with manual defending.

items.name: Role: Goalkeeper / Sweeper Keeper / Ball-Playing Keeper
items.detail: Goalkeeper stays on the line. Sweeper Keeper comes off the line to clear balls behind a high line (pairs with Aggressive/95 depth; Tekkz uses it). Ball-Playing Keeper joins build-up (Vejrgang uses it).

items.name: Role: Fullback / Wingback / Falseback / Inverted Wingback / Wide Back
items.detail: Fullback is the default balanced defender. Wingback and Attacking Wingback push high for width (in narrow formations they provide all the width). Falseback and Inverted Wingback tuck into midfield. Wide Back is a defensive wide CB-style role (sources dispute whether it is new).

items.name: Role: Defender / Stopper / Ball-Playing Defender
items.detail: CB roles. Defender holds the line. Stopper steps out aggressively to engage (risky with weak AI defending). Ball-Playing Defender progresses the ball in build-up.

items.name: Role: Holding / Centre-Half / Deep-Lying Playmaker
items.detail: CDM roles. Holding screens the back four (most-used defensive pairing). Centre-Half drops between the CBs. Deep-Lying Playmaker dictates build-up from deep. In 4-2-1-3 a common pairing is DLP plus Holding.

items.name: Role: Box-to-Box / Playmaker / Half-Winger / Box Crasher
items.detail: CM roles. Box-to-Box covers both boxes (Vejrgang and Tekkz CMs). Playmaker drifts to receive. Half-Winger drifts wide. Box Crasher makes late runs into the box (Dexerto pairs Holding plus Box Crasher).

items.name: Role: Shadow Striker / Classic 10 / Playmaker (CAM)
items.detail: Shadow Striker attacks the box like a second striker (the most common pro CAM role). Classic 10 stays central to create. Playmaker roams to receive.

items.name: Role: Winger / Inside Forward / Wide Playmaker
items.detail: Winger hugs the line and crosses. Inside Forward cuts into the half-space to shoot (meta in 4-2-1-3). Wide Playmaker drifts inside to create.

items.name: Role: Advanced Forward / Poacher / False 9 / Target Forward
items.detail: Advanced Forward (Attack focus) runs in behind and is the most-used ST role (about 60-65%). Poacher stays in the box. False 9 drops to link. Target Forward holds up and wins headers.

items.name: Role familiarity: Role+, Role++ and Versatile Focus
items.detail: Role+ and Role++ mark players suited to a role. In FC 27 all special cards automatically get Role++ in all positions within their primary and secondary roles. Out-of-position penalties are reportedly reduced, and a Versatile Focus option exists. EA has never published numeric effects. [Unverified]

items.name: Role count
items.detail: 37 position-role slots (about 30 distinct role names), carried over from FC 26. More alternate roles are promised during the year. The four roles often called new (Wide Back, Inverted Wingback, Box Crasher, Ball-Playing Keeper) were announced in FC 26.

items.name: PlayStyles overview
items.detail: 36 PlayStyle abilities (some GK-only). Gold PlayStyle+ is the stronger version. In FC 27 a card has a maximum of 3 PlayStyles+ (down from 5). EA's design aim is that attributes matter more, with a PlayStyle worth about 5-10%.

items.name: PlayStyle change: Finesse Shot
items.detail: Attributes (stats) now influence finesse outcomes more. Spin, animation speed and off-angle effectiveness were adjusted to shrink the gap for players without the PlayStyle. A high-Curve and Finishing player without it is closer than before.

items.name: PlayStyle change: Low Driven Shot
items.detail: Shot-speed boost removed: speed now comes from shooting attributes and input power only. The PlayStyle and PlayStyle+ still add accuracy. Low driven remains strong, especially at the near post.

items.name: PlayStyle change: Technical
items.detail: The gap between Technical and Technical+ was reduced; + still feels smoother. It improves Controlled Sprint dribbling.

items.name: PlayStyle change: Rapid
items.detail: The dribbling speed boost for PlayStyle owners is reduced. Non-PlayStyle players are unchanged, so raw Sprint Speed and Agility matter more.

items.name: PlayStyle change: Quick Step
items.detail: Smaller boost to acceleration and explosive dribbling. The Acceleration attribute matters more. Still helps the sprint-boost burst (R1/RB release then sprint).

items.name: PlayStyle change: Pinged Pass
items.detail: No longer reduces the receiver's trap error. It only affects the pass itself (fast, driven ground passes).

items.name: PlayStyle change: Tiki Taka
items.detail: FC 26's animation-speed boost and receiver trap boost were removed. It is now focused on quick combination one-touch play.

items.name: PlayStyle change: Jockey
items.detail: Smaller acceleration boost when leaving jockey. Non-PlayStyle players get faster jockey-sprint and acceleration, so all defenders can jockey better.

items.name: PlayStyle change: Intercept
items.detail: Players without Intercept but with high defensive attributes get more reach and success, so the PlayStyle's relative edge is smaller.

items.name: PlayStyle change: Precision Header
items.detail: The accuracy boost was rebalanced; the gap between Precision Header and + is reduced.

items.name: PlayStyle: First Touch
items.detail: Reduces error when trapping the ball and speeds the transition into dribbling. More valuable now that Tiki Taka and Pinged Pass no longer help receivers.

items.name: PlayStyle: Rush Out (GK)
items.detail: The keeper is faster when leaving the goal to close down an attacker. Useful behind a high line. Other GK PlayStyles include Far Reach, Footwork, Cross Claimer, Deflector and Far Throw. [Unverified]

items.name: PlayStyles Lab
items.detail: A FUT feature to add PlayStyles to items. The PlayStyle+ Lab returned around Future Stars Week 2 (from 17 Oct 2026). [Unverified]

items.name: Skill moves: star rating rule
items.detail: A player can only perform moves up to their Skill Moves star rating (1-5). In FC 27, 5-star moves were fixed in The Grounds (TU 1.0.1). Simplified Skill Moves is an option; pros turn it off.

items.name: Skill moves: new in FC 27 (disputed)
items.detail: The commonly cited new moves are Fake Turn (3 or 4 star), Ball Roll Spin (4 star), Stepover Combo (4 or 5 star) and Kneel Header (5 star, or 1 star needing the Trickster PlayStyle). Other lists add First Time Spin, Alternate Elastico Chop and Running Fake Drag (5 star). Counts range from 4 to 18 new entries. [Unverified]

items.name: Skill moves: 2-star examples
items.detail: Stop and Go, Drag to Drag, plus classic Stepover, Reverse Stepover, Body Feint, Ball Roll. Effective, simple direction changes (verify the in-game list). [Unverified]

items.name: Skill moves: 3-star examples
items.detail: Foot to Foot, Lateral Heel to Heel, Heel Chop, Roulette, Fake Left/Go Right, Ball Roll Cut, Drag Back, Spin. These are bread-and-butter evasion moves. [Unverified]

items.name: Skill moves: 4-star examples
items.detail: Drag Turn, Standing Scoop Turn, Flair Roulette, Four Touch Skill, Skilled Bridge, Drag to Chop, Ball Roll Spin, Fake Turn, plus Lane Change, Ball Roll Fake Turn, Elastico Chop, Heel to Ball Roll. [Unverified]

items.name: Skill moves: 5-star examples
items.detail: First Time Spin, Alternate Elastico Chop, Running Fake Drag, Stepover Combo, plus Elastico, Reverse Elastico, Advanced Rainbow, Tornado Spin, Ball Roll Flick, Flick Over. [Unverified]

items.name: Skill moves: practical use in FC 27
items.detail: With AI defenders no longer auto-tackling, simple direction changes (drag back, ball roll, stop-and-go, lane change) beat lunging users. Many users now jockey well, so do not spam skills into a set defender: use them when the defender commits. Practise in Training before using them online.

items.name: Role: Goalkeeper
items.detail: Goalkeeper: stays on the line. Sweeper Keeper: sweeps behind a high line. Ball-Playing Keeper: extra passer in build-up.

items.name: Role: Centre-back
items.detail: Defender: holds the line. Stopper: steps out to engage dropping forwards. Ball-Playing Defender: progresses the ball. Wide Back: back-three centre-back who covers wide (Support focus).

items.name: Role: Full-back
items.detail: Fullback (balanced default), Falseback (tucks into midfield), Wingback (width), Attacking Wingback (overlaps, Support/Attack), Inverted Wingback (moves into the half-space).

items.name: Role: Defensive midfield
items.detail: Holding: screens the back line (Defend or Roaming). Centre-Half: drops between centre-backs in build-up. Deep-Lying Playmaker: dictates from deep (Build-Up or Roaming).

items.name: Role: Central midfield
items.detail: Box-to-Box: both boxes. Holding and Deep-Lying Playmaker also available. Playmaker: drifts to receive. Half-Winger: drifts wide into the half-space. Box Crasher: late runs into the box.

items.name: Role: Wide midfield and wingers
items.detail: Winger: holds the touchline and crosses. Wide Midfielder: stays wide, links and defends, rarely attacks. Wide Playmaker: drifts inside to create. Inside Forward: cuts inside to shoot.

items.name: Role: Attacking midfield
items.detail: Playmaker, Shadow Striker (second-striker runs; usual pro pick), Half-Winger, Classic 10 (central creator).

items.name: Role: Striker
items.detail: Advanced Forward (runs in behind; most used), Poacher (box), False 9 (drops to link; Attack or Build-Up focus), Target Forward (hold-up and aerial; FC 27 presence not confirmed by FC 27 sources).

items.name: Role: Familiarity
items.detail: Role+ and Role++ mark suited players. In FC 27 every special item gets Role++ in all roles of its primary and secondary positions. EA has not published numeric effects. Counts: 37 position-role slots, about 30 role names (FUT.GG counts 31).

items.name: Formation: 4-3-1-2 on the radar
items.detail: Central diamond of three CMs and a CAM, two strikers close together, width only from full-backs. Weak against wide overloads and quick switches.

items.name: Formation: 4-2-1-3 on the radar
items.detail: Two holding markers just ahead of the back four, three forwards spread across the front line. Weak against central diamonds and overlapping full-backs.

items.name: Formation: 4-4-1-1 on the radar
items.detail: Two flat banks of four close together, a second striker just behind the striker. Solid against counters; can be passive.

items.name: Formation: Back five on the radar
items.detail: Five markers across the width of the box when defending; wing-backs push level with midfield in possession. Strongest protection of the box per guides, rarely used online.

items.name: Controller preset: Competitive
items.detail: The Competitive settings preset is the default in Ultimate Team and cannot be changed there, though individual settings can be adjusted in other modes. It uses Precision shot assistance by default.

items.name: Passing assistance settings
items.detail: Common pro setup: Ground, Cross and Lob passes Assisted; Through Pass Semi (direction follows your stick, power partly assisted) or Manual. Pass Receiver Lock set to Late.

items.name: Shot assistance
items.detail: Options are Assisted, Precision and Manual. Precision is the most common competitive pick. Red Bull recommends Assisted for players in Rivals Division 3 or lower until they master aiming. Turn Auto Shots off.

items.name: Switching settings
items.detail: Auto Switching: Air Balls and Loose Balls (or Manual). Right Stick Switching: Classic, Player Relative, sensitivity about 3-7. Next Player Switch Indicator on. Many pros (RBLZ Levy) prefer right-stick switching over L1/LB for precision.

items.name: Defending settings
items.detail: Advanced Defending (separate standing tackle and shoulder inputs) vs Tactical Defending (context-selects the tackle). Pass Block Assistance on, Professional Fouls on, Auto Clearances off (common pro list). Analog Sprint off.

items.name: Jockey (L2/LT)
items.detail: Hold to face the attacker side-on. FC 27 jockey speed is higher than FC 26 in Competitive gameplay (TU 1.0.1 also raised it in Authentic). Stay goal-side about 1 metre away and wait for a heavy touch.

items.name: Standing tackle (Circle/B)
items.detail: The default tackle; manual reach is longer than FC 26. Make one timed attempt, not three. R1+Circle (hard tackle) is risky. AI teammates no longer auto-tackle, so you must make it.

items.name: Slide tackle (Square/X)
items.detail: Last-resort tackle; a miss removes the defender from play, and mistimed slides give fouls, cards or penalties. Use it only when the standing tackle cannot reach.

items.name: Contain and Second Man Press
items.detail: Contain is X/A (Classic scheme). Teammate Contain or Second Man Press is R1/RB (hold, per most guides): one AI teammate closes the ball carrier while you cover the passing lane or runner. Do not pull CBs out with it. [Unverified]

items.name: Shoulder challenge (anti-spam)
items.detail: Repeated shoulder-challenge presses now make the defender stick an arm out and slow down. Spamming it is punished. Use single, timed challenges when side by side.

items.name: Team Press
items.detail: Team-wide pressing for a limited time. In FC 27 it has NO effect while the ball is in your defensive third. Use it in the middle or final third after losing possession. It drains stamina.

items.name: Manual switching priority
items.detail: With weaker AI defenders, switching early to the right defender before the danger arrives is essential. Switching to a CB too early drops the line and opens space (RBLZ Levy).

items.name: Through pass (Triangle/Y)
items.detail: Follows your aimed direction strictly in FC 27. Aim at the space the runner will reach, not at the runner. Power and direction both matter. Precision Through Pass is R1+Triangle / RB+Y.

items.name: Dinked / lofted through pass
items.detail: Dinked pass is now only on double-tap Through Pass and is fully manual. A lobbed through (L1+Triangle / LB+Y) beats a high line. Guides disagree on some double-tap labels. [Unverified]

items.name: Driven ground pass (R1+X / RB+A)
items.detail: A fast pass between midfielders to break a press. Do not drive it into a tightly marked striker.

items.name: Crossing (Square/X)
items.detail: Less assisted: crosses drop into the space you aim at. Cross ahead of the attacker's run rather than at the body. Whipped and driven crosses have variants. Clean header contact needs precise timing.

items.name: Triggered run (L1/LB)
items.detail: Sends a teammate on a direct run. In FC 27 manual runs stop after a limited distance and players return to position; retrigger if needed.

items.name: Triggered Curved Run (tap L1+R1 / LB+RB)
items.detail: New in FC 27: the selected teammate bends the run around defenders into open space. Strong against flat high lines to stay onside, then cut in.

items.name: Pass & Follow Run (L1+R1+X / LB+RB+A)
items.detail: New in FC 27: pass, and the passer immediately makes a curved follow-up run, giving a quick one-two route.

items.name: Avoidance (hold R1/RB on corners)
items.detail: New: during the corner positioning window, the controlled attacker or defender slips through crowds without being blocked. Some guides list it as R1+Left Stick. [Unverified]

items.name: Shielding (hold L2/LT)
items.detail: Holds position or protects the ball. On corners, after Avoidance, hold Shielding to anchor your attacker so defenders cannot step in front. Throw-ins also gain Shielding and Avoidance.

items.name: Set-piece tactics (D-pad Up)
items.detail: Free kicks and corners carry pre-set player instructions. The corner tactics menu moved from D-pad Down to D-pad Up. The FC 26 options 'Edge of Box Run' and 'Crowd the Goalkeeper' were removed in favour of adding or removing players.

items.name: Corners: three steps
items.detail: 1) Aim and deliver. 2) Move your attacker with Avoidance and Shielding into a spot (no auto-positioning). 3) Time the header or volley. Defenders must also manually switch and mark in crowded boxes.

items.name: Shot types overview
items.detail: Standard (Circle/B), Finesse (R1+Circle), Power Shot (L1+R1+Circle), Chip (L1+Circle), Low Driven (double-tap shoot), Low Driven Finesse (R1+shoot, shoot) and Low Driven Power (L1+R1+shoot, shoot). Timed finishing has not returned since FC 26 removed it.

items.name: Low driven shot
items.detail: Double-tap shoot, with the second press right after the first. It no longer gains extra speed from the PlayStyle; speed comes from attributes and power. Best inside the box, in 1v1s and toward bottom corners. EA acknowledges near-post low drivens are strong.

items.name: Finesse shot
items.detail: R1/RB+shoot: curled placement to the far corner. Outcomes depend more on the Curve and Finishing attributes now. Use it from the edge of the box at an angle, with space.

items.name: Power shot
items.detail: L1+R1 (LB+RB)+shoot. Slow wind-up, high speed. Best from range with a clear lane; avoid it under pressure in a crowded box. Turn Power Shot Zoom off.

items.name: Dribbling: Controlled Sprint
items.detail: Sits between slow dribble and full sprint. Use it near the box and release it before sharp turns. The Technical PlayStyle improves it.

items.name: Dribbling: sprint touches
items.detail: Full sprint lengthens touches, so direction changes get harder. Over-sprinting is a top mistake: walk into space first.

items.name: Dribbling: sprint boost
items.detail: Hold R1/RB for tight touches, release, then tap sprint for an explosive burst. Quick Step helps, though less after its nerf.

items.name: Dribbling: off-balance dribbling (new)
items.detail: When a physical challenge knocks an agile dribbler off balance, they can keep the ball and choose the next touch. It favours Agility, Balance and Dribbling, but timing and body position matter.

items.name: Dribbling: shielding and stop-and-go
items.detail: Slow down to make the defender settle into a jockey, then accelerate when they commit. Small first touches beat compact blocks; take big touches only into open space.

items.name: AI attacking spatial awareness
items.detail: AI runners read space, defensive shape and the offside line, e.g. a winger stays level with the last defender, then curves in when the pass is played. It works alongside Player Roles, which still define run types.

items.name: AI defending behaviour (Competitive)
items.detail: AI defenders hold positional shape and block lanes but rarely start tackles. They react to nearby loose balls. Interception ranges for passive AI were reduced. The user must provide the pressure.

items.name: Defensive Approach and Line Height
items.detail: Deep 1-30 (default 25): drops with runs, no pressure. Balanced 31-60 (50): flexible. High 61-90 (70): situational pressure, may not track runs. Aggressive 91-100 (95): presses immediately after losing the ball, plays an offside trap, extra stamina drain.

items.name: Build-Up Style
items.detail: Three options: Short Passing (patient, players come short), Balanced (default, most used) and Counter (direct, runners go early). Tekkz reportedly uses Counter with a 4-3-1-2 line 60. [Unverified]

items.name: In-match tactics: My Tactics (D-pad Left)
items.detail: Switch between up to 5 saved Custom Tactics. Each can change formation, Build-Up, Defensive Approach, Player Roles and Focuses without pausing. It takes a moment to apply.

items.name: In-match tactics: Tactical Focus (D-pad Right)
items.detail: Default, Attacking or Defending: temporarily shifts build-up, defensive approach and compatible role focuses without changing the formation or roles or editing the saved tactic. Use Defending to protect a late lead.

items.name: Player stamina and fatigue
items.detail: Sprinting, pressing (Team Press, Aggressive approach) and long matches drain stamina. The player indicator can fade with stamina. Make subs at about 60-70 minutes for pressing players. [Unverified]

items.name: Professional fouls
items.detail: When on, a defender can deliberately foul to stop a counter at the cost of a card risk. Commonly enabled by pros.

items.name: Goalkeeper control
items.detail: Manual GK rush (Triangle/Y hold) and GK switch exist. The 1v1 GK holding-ball bug was fixed in TU 1.1.0. Watch for keepers left exposed at the near post. [Unverified]

items.name: Visual settings that help
items.detail: 2D radar with team-coloured dots, Player Name Large indicator, Next Player Switch Indicator on, camera shake off, Power Shot Zoom off. Path: Settings > Game Settings > R1/RB to Visual Settings.

items.name: Skill moves: Pad mapping
items.detail: Inputs are the same on PlayStation and Xbox apart from labels: L1=LB, R1=RB, L2=LT, R2=RT, R3=right stick click, Cross=A, Circle=B, Square=X, Triangle=Y. RS = right stick, LS = left stick. Star tiers for some moves differ between guides.

items.name: Skill moves: 1 star
items.detail: Ball Juggle (standing): hold L2 / LT, tap R1 / RB. Directional Nutmeg: hold L1+R1 / LB+RB, move RS. Giant Fake Shot (new, one source): L2 / LT + fake shot while standing. Kneel Header: 1 star with Trickster per one source, 5 star per others.

items.name: Skill moves: 2 star
items.detail: Body Feint: flick RS left or right (direction label disputed). Stepover: rotate RS from up to left or right. Reverse Stepover: rotate RS from left or right to up. Ball Roll: hold RS left or right. Feint Forward and Turn: flick RS down twice. Drag Back: L1+R1 / LB+RB + flick LS down (some list L2 + hold RS down). Stop and Go, Drag to Drag (inputs not confirmed).

items.name: Skill moves: 3 star
items.detail: Heel Flick: flick RS up then down. Roulette: rotate RS from down round to left or right. Fake Left and Go Right: rotate RS left, down, right (mirror for the other side). Heel Chop (running): L2 / LT with fake shot, then LS direction. Foot to Foot, Lateral Heel to Heel (inputs not confirmed). Fake Turn (new; 3 or 4 star).

items.name: Skill moves: 4 star
items.detail: Ball Hop (standing): hold L1 / LB, press R3. Lane Change: hold L1 / LB, hold RS left or right. Simple Rainbow: flick RS down, up, up. Spin: hold R1 / RB, rotate RS 270 degrees (disputed). Fake Pass (standing): R2 / RT + Square or Circle (X or B), then Cross / A. Three Touch Roulette: hold L2 / LT, flick RS down then left or right (4 or 5 star). Flair Roulette, Ball Roll Spin (new).

items.name: Skill moves: 5 star
items.detail: Elastico: rotate RS right, down, left. Reverse Elastico: left, down, right. Advanced Rainbow: flick RS down, hold up, flick up. Tornado Spin: hold L1 / LB, flick RS up then left or right. Ball Roll and Flick (running): hold RS left or right, then flick RS up. Heel Flick Turn: hold L2+R1 / LT+RB, flick RS up then down. Stepover Combo (new; 4 or 5 star).

items.name: Skill moves: 5 star, new or unconfirmed inputs
items.detail: First Time Spin, Alternate Elastico Chop and Running Fake Drag (Keymap lists them at 5 star; inputs not confirmed). Kneel Header (5 star in most lists). Sombrero flicks while juggling: hold L2+R1 / LT+RB with LS direction (Driffle). TU 1.0.1 fixed 5-star moves not working in street matches.

items.name: Skill moves: Which moves matter
items.detail: Most useful competitively: ball roll, drag back, lane change, heel chop, stepover and roulette. Use them against one committed defender with space behind them; pass into crowds.

items.name: Set pieces: Corner sequence
items.detail: 1) Aim and deliver. 2) Camera turns to the box for a brief window: move your attacker with Avoidance (hold R1 / RB) and hold the spot with Shielding (hold L2 / LT). 3) Time the header or volley. Attackers no longer auto-position.

items.name: Set pieces: Corner tactics
items.detail: D-pad Up (moved from D-pad Down): add or remove runners, near or far post. FC 26's Edge of Box Run and Crowd the Goalkeeper were replaced by adding or removing players.

items.name: Set pieces: Defending corners
items.detail: Select your best header before delivery and use Avoidance to beat screens. Keep the six-yard box and the penalty spot covered; FC 27 crosses land in space more often.

items.name: Set pieces: Free kick mechanics
items.detail: Place the reticle on goal, drag the marker across the ball to set spin and lift, then hold for power (framework from FC 24). Dead-centre plus high power gives a knuckleball; striking high on the ball keeps it flat. High Shot Power needs less of the bar.

items.name: Set pieces: Free kick takers
items.detail: EA names Free Kick Accuracy, Curve and Shot Power. One guide recommends assigning a left-footed and a right-footed taker for each side. Vary power with distance.

items.name: Set pieces: Free kick tactics
items.detail: D-pad Up: add or remove runners, send players near or far post, choose zonal or player marking. Use the indirect routine from wide positions.

items.name: Set pieces: Penalties
items.detail: Guide advice: choose a low corner, use about half the power bar, commit before the run-up. Composure and Penalties matter more than Finishing. Practise in Skill Games (Precision Penalty) and the Training Centre.

items.name: Set pieces: Throw-ins
items.detail: FC 27 adds Shielding and Avoidance for throw-in receivers.

items.name: Set pieces: Exploits to ignore
items.detail: A deep free-kick exploit was fixed server-side by Live Update #1 (14-15 Oct). A goalkeeper scoring from free kicks in their own box was reported. Never advise either.

items.name: Default competitive tactic template
items.detail: Balanced build-up, Balanced defensive approach, line height about 55-61, two holding-type midfielders (CDM pair or Holding plus Box-to-Box). This is the community and pro baseline in FC 27 because AI defending is weaker.

items.name: Vejrgang's 4-3-1-2 (FUTSettings)
items.detail: Balanced build-up, Balanced approach, line 60. GK Ball-Playing Keeper; LB and RB Fullback; CBs Defender; CMs two Box-to-Box plus one Holding; CAM Shadow Striker; STs Advanced Forward x2. [Unverified]

items.name: Tekkz 4-3-1-2 / 4-4-1-1
items.detail: FUTSettings lists Tekkz in a 4-3-1-2 with Counter build-up, Balanced approach, line 60, Sweeper Keeper, Fullbacks, Defenders, Box-to-Box CMs, Shadow Striker and two Advanced Forwards. Red Bull quotes them recommending a 4-4-1-1 with adjusted roles. The sources conflict. [Unverified]

items.name: RedLac's 4-3-1-2 (Red Bull)
items.detail: Drops wide players to bolster central midfield; focus attack and defence through the centre. Line height and roles not published.

items.name: NealGuides 4-2-1-3
items.detail: ST Advanced Forward, wide Inside Forwards, CAM Shadow Striker, CDMs Deep-Lying Playmaker plus Holding, Fullbacks, Defenders. Codes conflict across pages, so test in-game.

items.name: Aggressive 95 depth meta
items.detail: Since around two weeks after launch many lobbies run Aggressive (default 95) with an extreme high press and offside trap. The depth slider acts more directly on the line, manual runs are capped, and through balls are less assisted, which makes the trap strong. EA has announced no change.

items.name: How to beat 95 depth / high press
items.detail: Short triangles (CB to CDM to CM) to draw the presser out before playing forward. Switch play to the far side when they overload one side. Lobbed through balls into space behind the line, timed before the striker goes offside. Curved runs to stay onside. Driven passes into midfield, not into a marked ST.

items.name: Using 95 depth safely
items.detail: You need fast CBs to recover when the trap breaks, plus a Sweeper Keeper. Watch stamina (Aggressive drains more). Drop to High (about 70) or Balanced (60) when leading or when CBs are slow.

items.name: How to beat narrow formations (4-3-1-2, 4-1-2-1-2)
items.detail: Their weakness is width. Isolate their fullbacks with wingers or wide overloads, switch play quickly before they shift, cross early, then attack the centre once their midfield is pulled wide. Avoid forcing passes into the packed middle. [Unverified]

items.name: How to beat a deep block / park the bus
items.detail: Stretch the pitch with width, vary the tempo (patient circulation, then sudden one-twos), attack the CB-FB gap, use cut-backs and near-post low drivens, shoot from range for rebounds, and treat corners as a weapon with the new manual positioning. [Unverified]

items.name: How to beat counter-attack teams
items.detail: Keep two holding midfielders (4-2-1-3, 4-2-3-1) and avoid committing fullbacks at the same time. Use professional fouls on breaks. Jockey and delay rather than diving in. Keep the line Balanced (about 55-60).

items.name: Defending in FC 27: priorities
items.detail: 1) Switch early to the right player. 2) Jockey goal-side and keep your distance. 3) One timed standing tackle. 4) Use Second Man Press sparingly. 5) Never pull CBs out of the line. 6) Team Press only outside your defensive third.

items.name: Build-up under pressure
items.detail: Stay composed: frantic pass mashing causes misplaced passes. Pass in the direction the player is facing. Use a DLP or Ball-Playing Defender to recycle. Driven ground passes beat a press between the lines (Red Bull pro tips).

items.name: Game-state management
items.detail: Leading late: Tactical Focus Defending (D-pad Right), swap to a saved 5-back or deeper tactic (D-pad Left), lower the line, keep the ball. Chasing: Tactical Focus Attacking, add a striker, raise the line and use Team Press in the middle third.

items.name: Corner attacking routine
items.detail: Deliver to a zone (near post or penalty spot), use Avoidance to escape your marker, Shielding to hold the spot, then time the header. Mix short corners if their box is crowded.

items.name: Corner defending routine
items.detail: Manually select the most dangerous marker before delivery, use Avoidance to beat screens, stay goal-side and contest. Auto-switching on air balls helps some users.

items.name: Squad building for FC 27
items.detail: Attributes matter more than PlayStyles now. Prioritise Pace, Acceleration, Agility and Balance for dribblers, Defensive Awareness and Standing Tackle for CBs, and Curve and Finishing for finessers. Fast CBs are key behind high lines. A card has at most 3 PlayStyles+.

items.name: Rivals weekly plan
items.detail: Reach 30 points for the Upgrade reward (10 wins). Win streaks speed up promotion. Stop when tilted. CQP from your division helps reach Champions (1,000 needed).

items.name: Squad Battles efficiency
items.detail: Play one difficulty above your comfort level vs lower-rated squads and drop for strong ones. Score up to 5 goals. Never quit early (0 points). Win on World Class for the CQP objective.

items.name: Champions weekend plan
items.detail: 15 matches, so spread them across Friday to Monday. Rewards are by wins, with coins starting at 5 wins. Avoid long tilt runs; review losses between games.

items.name: Half-time coaching checklist
items.detail: Compare possession, shots and xG. Is the opponent's line high (radar)? Are you losing the ball centrally (possession lost heat map)? Change one thing: line height, build-up style or a role focus.

items.name: Exploiting the near post
items.detail: When the keeper cheats toward the far post or you have a tight angle, the near-post low driven shot is the highest-percentage finish in FC 27 (EA-acknowledged). As a defender, block the near-post lane.

items.name: Career mode tactics
items.detail: 4-2-1-3 with DLP or Holding CDMs, or a 4-4-2 Flat balanced system, are recommended. Authentic gameplay makes teammates less likely to run in behind automatically, so trigger runs more.

items.name: Rush and small-sided play
items.detail: Spacing matters more than skill: keep one player back, use quick one-twos, and exploit the AI GK with low driven shots. Rush-specific rules can be checked in the in-game tutorial. [Unverified]

items.name: Tactics: Team tactics in FC IQ
items.detail: Two team settings: Build-Up Style (Short Passing, Balanced, Counter) and Defensive Approach with Line Height (Deep 1-30, Balanced up to 60, High 61-90, Aggressive 91-100). Everything else comes from each player's Role and Focus.

items.name: Tactics: Defaults
items.detail: Deep 25, Balanced 50, High 70, Aggressive 95 (FIFA Ultimate Team guide). Most pros run Balanced at 60; Red Bull quotes Tekkz and RedLac at 61-65; Boosting Market says 44% of pro squads now push the line to High.

items.name: Tactics: Depth tuning in FC 27
items.detail: Closed-beta change: at low depth defenders retreat earlier and hold conservative positions. At 95 the line pushes as high as possible and presses at once after losing the ball.

items.name: Tactics: Set-piece tactics
items.detail: D-pad Up at corners and free kicks: add or remove runners, near or far post, zonal or player marking. Plan rest defence here too.

items.name: Tactics: Tactical Focus vs My Tactics
items.detail: Tactical Focus (D-pad Right) temporarily shifts build-up, approach and compatible role focuses. My Tactics (D-pad Left) swaps whole saved tactics including formation and roles. Both take a moment to apply.

items.name: Tactics: Choosing build-up
items.detail: Short Passing suits a 4-4-1-1 built for central combinations (Tekkz); Balanced suits most 4-3-1-2 and 4-2-1-3 builds; Counter suits two fast strikers against high lines.

items.name: Tactics: Line height and pace
items.detail: Higher lines need fast centre-backs and a Sweeper Keeper. Guides suggest 50-55 while learning manual defending and about 40-50 to protect a lead.

items.name: Waiting for AI teammates to win the ball
items.detail: In FC 27 AI defenders no longer auto-tackle. Fix: switch to the nearest defender, jockey and make a timed standing tackle yourself.

items.name: Spamming tackle or shoulder challenge
items.detail: Multiple presses lead to missed tackles, and spammed shoulder challenges now slow the defender. Fix: one timed tackle after a heavy touch.

items.name: Pulling centre-backs out of the line
items.detail: Pressing with a CB opens the space behind. Fix: press with midfielders or Second Man Press and keep CBs in the line.

items.name: Switching too late (or to a CB too early)
items.detail: Late switches leave runners free, and switching to a CB too early drops the line. Fix: anticipate and switch before the pass; prefer right-stick switching for precision.

items.name: Using Team Press in your own third
items.detail: It does nothing there in FC 27. Fix: press after losing the ball in the middle or final third.

items.name: Over-sprinting
items.detail: Holding sprint lengthens touches and causes turnovers. Fix: cut sprint use by about 30%, walk into space, and use Controlled Sprint near the box.

items.name: Through balls aimed at the runner
items.detail: FC 27 through balls follow your aim strictly. Fix: aim at the space ahead of the run and control power; practise in Training.

items.name: Crossing at the striker's body
items.detail: Crosses land in the aimed space. Fix: cross ahead of the run into space and time the header.

items.name: Expecting auto-positioning on corners
items.detail: Attackers do not move to the best spot. Fix: use Avoidance and Shielding during the positioning window.

items.name: Relying on PlayStyles over attributes
items.detail: PlayStyles are worth about 5-10% now. Fix: pick players for core attributes (pace, agility, shooting, defending).

items.name: Power shots under pressure
items.detail: Long wind-up shots get blocked in a crowded box. Fix: low driven or finesse in the box; power shots only with a clear lane from range.

items.name: Ignoring the near post
items.detail: Users always aim far post. Fix: check whether the GK has opened the near post and take the low driven.

items.name: Changing everything after one loss
items.detail: Overreacting hides the real issue. Fix: identify the repeated failure (e.g. 2v1s on one flank) and adjust one setting.

items.name: Buying cards to fix an undiagnosed problem
items.detail: Fix: review match facts and replays first to see whether the problem is squad or execution.

items.name: Line too high with slow CBs
items.detail: 95 depth with slow CBs gets beaten by lobbed throughs. Fix: lower to about 60-70 or buy faster CBs plus a Sweeper Keeper.

items.name: Forcing the ball into a narrow block
items.detail: Fix: switch play wide, use fullbacks and overloads, and cut back.

items.name: Not using the radar
items.detail: Runs outside the camera are missed. Fix: use the 2D radar with team colours and glance often.

items.name: Frantic passing in build-up
items.detail: Mashing pass causes misplaced balls. Fix: composure; pass in the direction the player faces.

items.name: Mistimed slide tackles
items.detail: A miss removes the defender and risks cards or penalties. Fix: standing tackle by default; slide only as a last resort.

items.name: Quitting Squad Battles early
items.detail: Ending a match early gives 0 Battle Points. Fix: finish matches.

items.name: Not trigger-running in Authentic or Career
items.detail: Authentic AI makes fewer automatic runs in behind. Fix: use L1 runs and curved runs.

items.name: Using exploits (e.g. deep free-kick glitch)
items.detail: Exploits are patched (Live Update #1) and can risk account action. The coach must never recommend glitches. Fix: practise legitimate set pieces.

items.name: Leaving Pass Receiver Lock on Default
items.detail: Control switches to the receiver too early. Fix: set it to Late.

items.name: Tilting through a weekend
items.detail: Fix: take breaks between Champions games, review the last loss's Match Facts, and stop after 3 straight losses. [Unverified]

items.name: TU (Title Update)
items.detail: A downloadable patch (e.g. 1.0.4, 1.1.0) that goes through console certification.

items.name: Live Update
items.detail: A server-side tuning or fix applied by restarting the game, with no download (e.g. Live Update #1 free-kick fix).

items.name: Pitch Notes
items.detail: EA's official developer blog posts about gameplay and modes (Gameplay Deep Dive, Launch Update, and so on).

items.name: Competitive gameplay
items.detail: The online gameplay ruleset (FUT, Rivals, Champions) with reduced AI defending.

items.name: Authentic Gameplay 2.0
items.detail: The offline and realistic ruleset (Career, Kick-Off) with expanded sliders.

items.name: CQP
items.detail: Champions Qualification Points; 1,000 needed to enter FUT Champions Finals.

items.name: Champs / Weekend League
items.detail: FUT Champions Finals: 15 matches over a weekend.

items.name: Rivals
items.detail: Division Rivals, the weekly ranked FUT online mode.

items.name: SBC
items.detail: Squad Building Challenge: exchange items for rewards.

items.name: Evo
items.detail: Evolution: upgrade path for an item via objectives (Pathways in FC 27).

items.name: SP
items.detail: Season Points that level the Season Pass; 850/day cap from matches.

items.name: TOTW
items.detail: Team of the Week special items.

items.name: OVR
items.detail: Overall rating; in Career FC 27 it is dynamic with form, morale and fitness.

items.name: xG
items.detail: Expected goals: shot-quality measure shown in Match Facts.

items.name: Chem
items.detail: Chemistry: FUT link bonus from club, league and nation (0-3 per player).

items.name: PlayStyle / PlayStyle+
items.detail: Special abilities; + is the elite version (max 3 per item in FC 27).

items.name: Role / Role+ / Role++
items.detail: Player Role tactical behaviour and familiarity levels.

items.name: Focus
items.detail: Sub-setting of a role (e.g. Attack, Balanced, Defend, Build-Up).

items.name: Depth / line height
items.detail: Defensive line height slider 1-100 (Aggressive default 95).

items.name: Build-Up Style
items.detail: Short Passing, Balanced or Counter.

items.name: Defensive Approach
items.detail: Deep, Balanced, High or Aggressive.

items.name: Jockey
items.detail: Side-on defending stance (L2/LT).

items.name: Second Man Press / Teammate Contain
items.detail: Teammate presses the ball carrier (R1/RB).

items.name: Team Press
items.detail: Temporary team-wide press; inactive in your own defensive third in FC 27.

items.name: Low driven (LD)
items.detail: Double-tap shoot for a low, accurate shot.

items.name: Finesse shot
items.detail: R1/RB+shoot placed curling shot, usually to the far corner.

items.name: Curved Run
items.detail: New FC 27 triggered run that bends into space (L1+R1).

items.name: Pass & Follow
items.detail: New FC 27 run where the passer follows up (L1+R1+X).

items.name: Avoidance
items.detail: New FC 27 input to slip through crowds before corner delivery.

items.name: Shielding
items.detail: Protect the ball or hold position (L2/LT).

items.name: Off-balance dribbling
items.detail: New FC 27 recovery dribble after physical contact.

items.name: Dinked pass
items.detail: Chipped pass on double-tap Through Pass.

items.name: Inside Forward (IF)
items.detail: Wide forward role cutting inside.

items.name: Shadow Striker (SS)
items.detail: CAM role making runs like a second striker.

items.name: DLP
items.detail: Deep-Lying Playmaker CDM role.

items.name: B2B
items.detail: Box-to-Box CM role.

items.name: AF
items.detail: Advanced Forward striker role.

items.name: The Grounds
items.detail: FC 27 open-world social hub that houses Clubs.

items.name: AXP
items.detail: Archetype XP, the Grounds and Clubs progression currency.

items.name: Amps / Masteries
items.detail: Grounds progression: temporary modifiers and permanent archetype boosts.

items.name: FC IQ
items.detail: The tactics system introduced in FC 25: roles, focuses and smart tactics.

items.name: Meta
items.detail: Most effective, commonly used tactics or players at a given time.

items.name: Sweat
items.detail: Slang for an ultra-try-hard meta playstyle.

items.name: Tilt
items.detail: Playing worse due to frustration after losses.

items.name: FC Pro
items.detail: EA's official esports circuit (Open, World Championship).

items.name: Radar
items.detail: The in-match mini-map showing players and the ball (also called the mini-map).

items.name: 2D radar
items.detail: Flat top-down radar; distances map linearly to the pitch.

items.name: 3D radar
items.detail: Tilted perspective radar; distances are compressed toward the far side.

items.name: User Radar Colour
items.detail: Setting for your team's radar markers (Default plus seven colours).

items.name: Opponent Radar Colour
items.detail: Setting for the opponent's radar markers.

items.name: Score Clock
items.detail: The top-left score and time display; can be switched off.

items.name: Score Clock Dropdown
items.detail: Information panel that drops below the score clock; can be switched off.

items.name: Next Player Switch Indicator
items.detail: Marker above the defender L1 / LB will switch to.

items.name: Player Name Bar
items.detail: Bottom-screen bar with the controlled player's name and stamina, with optional PlayStyles+, skill stars and footedness.

items.name: High Contrast Gameplay
items.detail: Accessibility mode that recolours players, keepers, referee and ball for visibility.

items.name: Line height (metres)
items.detail: Distance from your goal line to your deepest outfield player; in FC also the 1-100 depth slider.

items.name: Low block
items.detail: Defending deep, roughly within 25-35 m of your own goal.

items.name: Mid block
items.detail: Defending with the line roughly 35-45 m from goal, engaging in midfield.

items.name: High block / high press
items.detail: Defending with a high line, often 50 m or more from goal, pressing early.

items.name: Compactness
items.detail: Short distances within and between lines when defending.

items.name: Team length
items.detail: Distance between the deepest and most advanced outfield player.

items.name: Team width
items.detail: Distance between the two widest outfield players.

items.name: Rest defence
items.detail: Players kept behind the ball while attacking to stop counters, usually one more than their forwards.

items.name: Counter-press
items.detail: Pressing straight after losing the ball to win it back quickly.

items.name: Pressing trigger
items.detail: A cue to press: back pass, poor touch, ball to the touchline, receiver facing their own goal.

items.name: PPDA
items.detail: Passes allowed per defensive action; lower means more intense pressing.

items.name: Ball Recovery Time
items.detail: Seconds taken to win the ball back after losing it; on the FC Match Facts summary.

items.name: Half-space
items.detail: Vertical channel between the touchline lane and the centre.

items.name: Zone 14
items.detail: Central area just outside the penalty box.

items.name: Overload
items.detail: More of your players than theirs in one area.

items.name: Isolation
items.detail: A one against one created on the far side after an overload.

items.name: Overlap
items.detail: A run around the outside of the ball carrier.

items.name: Underlap
items.detail: A run inside the ball carrier, between them and the centre.

items.name: Third-man run
items.detail: A run by a third player into space created by a two-player exchange.

items.name: Blind-side run
items.detail: A run behind a defender's back, out of their view.

items.name: Cutback
items.detail: A pass pulled back from near the byline to a player arriving in the box.

items.name: Box occupancy
items.detail: How many attackers or defenders are in the key box zones when the ball arrives.

items.name: Switch of play
items.detail: A pass moving the ball quickly to the opposite flank.

items.name: Transition
items.detail: The seconds after the ball changes hands.

items.name: Second ball
items.detail: The loose ball after a header, clearance or block.

items.name: xG per shot
items.detail: Average expected goals per shot; a measure of chance quality.

items.name: Big chance
items.detail: A shot with a high scoring probability, such as a tap-in or a one-on-one.

items.name: Player Lock
items.detail: FC mechanic to control an off-ball player; tuned in FC 27.

items.name: Ground Cross
items.detail: Cross along the ground (Square twice / X twice).

items.name: Lobbed Through Pass
items.detail: Through ball over the line (L1+Triangle / LB+Y).

items.name: Tactical Focus
items.detail: D-pad Right: Default, Attacking or Defending focus without editing the tactic.

items.name: My Tactics
items.detail: D-pad Left: switch between up to five saved custom tactics.

items.name: Tactical Vision
items.detail: Manager Career template for a team's playstyle.

items.name: House Rules
items.detail: Kick-Off and event rule variants such as Survival and Mystery Ball.

items.name: Survival
items.detail: House Rule where a scoring team loses an outfield player after each goal.

items.name: Mystery Ball
items.detail: House Rule where the ball returns with one of five temporary effects.

items.name: Kickabout
items.detail: Casual small-sided game in The Grounds.

items.name: Drop-In
items.detail: Matchmade Clubs game joined as an individual.

items.name: EA Javelin
items.detail: EA's PC anticheat that blocks denylisted software.

items.name: Offside trap
items.detail: Stepping the back line up together to leave attackers offside; strong with 95 depth, beaten by well-timed runs.

items.name: Knuckleball
items.detail: Free kick struck dead-centre with high power so it dips and moves unpredictably.

items.name: Line-breaking pass
items.detail: A pass that travels past an opposition line of players to a teammate behind it.

items.name: Pinning
items.detail: Keeping defenders occupied with forwards so they cannot help elsewhere.

items.name: Rest attack
items.detail: Players the defending team leaves high to threaten a counter.

items.name: 95 depth
items.detail: Aggressive defensive approach at its default line height; the FC 27 high-line meta.

formations.name: Pro 4-3-1-2 (Balanced, line 60)
formations.roles: GK Ball-Playing Keeper or Sweeper Keeper; LB/RB Fullback (Balanced); CBs Defender (Defend); CMs Holding in the middle (77% of pros per one guide) with two Box-to-Box; CAM Shadow Striker; two STs Advanced Forward.
formations.who: Most-used pro shape: 31% of pro squads on FUT.GG's overview (43% on its formation page). Vejrgang's listed setup matches it (FUTSettings). RedLac recommends a 4-3-1-2 in Red Bull's guide.
formations.radarLook: No wide players: in possession you see a central diamond of four markers plus two strikers close together; full-back markers provide all the width. Out of possession a narrow back four with three midfielders close in front.
strengths: Central overload and quick striker-CAM triangles
Holding CM screens the back four
weaknesses: No natural width; full-backs isolated against wingers
Long switches find their far full-back alone
Full-backs who push on leave the channels open
counters: Hold width on both touchlines and switch early before their midfield slides
Overlap your full-back to make two against one on their full-back
Keep two holding players so their striker-CAM triangle meets numbers
Cross early to the far post while their narrow back line is shifting

formations.roles: Sweeper Keeper, Fullbacks, Defenders, Box-to-Box CMs, Shadow Striker, two Advanced Forwards (FUTSettings listing for Tekkz).

formations.radarLook: Strikers start high on the last line; after a regain the two striker markers sprint beyond the line at once.
weaknesses: Gives the ball back quickly
Midfield can be outnumbered if both CMs join
counters: Keep a rest defence of two centre-backs plus a holding midfielder
Drop your line to about 55-60 so their runners have less space
Keep the ball longer to tire their pressing strikers

formations.name: Aggressive 95 depth high line (any shape, often 4-3-1-2)
formations.roles: Needs fast centre-backs and a Sweeper Keeper; Shadow Striker CAM in the EasySBC version.
formations.who: Widespread in lobbies about two weeks after launch (Timesaver); EasySBC's 12 Oct 4-3-1-2 build uses it and warns the space behind is the risk. Boosting Market: 44% of pro squads now push the line High vs 30% of the community.
formations.radarLook: Their deepest defender marker sits near halfway, often 45-55 m from their goal; their keeper marker stays near the box. The whole team is squeezed into about 30-35 m.
strengths: Immediate press after losing the ball
weaknesses: Huge space behind the line
Stamina drain
Slow centre-backs are exposed to balls over the top
counters: Lobbed through ball (L1+Triangle / LB+Y) into the channel as your runner starts level with the last defender
Triggered Curved Run to stay onside and bend in behind
Short triangles to draw the press, then a driven pass into midfield
Switch play to the far side when they squeeze one flank
Pick quick forwards; use a midfielder with Long Ball Pass

formations.name: 4-2-1-3 (Balanced, line 60)
formations.roles: CDMs Deep-Lying Playmaker plus Holding; CAM Playmaker or Shadow Striker; LW/RW Inside Forward; ST Advanced Forward; Fullbacks; Defenders.
formations.who: Most-used community formation (about 25-29% of squads on FUT.GG in October); 16-17% of pros.
formations.radarLook: Two midfield markers sit just in front of the back four; three forwards spread across the front line with the wide forwards starting near the touchlines and cutting inside.
strengths: Two holding midfielders cover for weak AI defending
weaknesses: Only one central creator; can be outnumbered by a diamond
Wide forwards may not track full-backs
counters: Overload the centre with a 4-3-1-2 or 4-1-2-1-2 so their two CDMs face three or four
Attack with overlapping full-backs when their wide forwards do not track
Use runs from your wingers when their full-back steps toward the ball (FUT.GG tip)

limitations: Frames are sampled about every 2.5 seconds, so many turnovers are missed; turnover maps show a sample, not every lost ball.
Goal locations come from replays on the broadcast camera and are approximate (six zones).
Goals are counted from scoreboard changes; if the scoreboard cannot be read, goals may be missed.
Pass accuracy and possession come from the statistics screen, so they are only known if that screen is shown.
The radar is read from the screen in 2D only; with the 3D radar the positions are skewed, so nothing is measured. With the radar Off there is no pitch analysis.
How FC draws the ball and the player you control on the radar is not documented; reading is tuned on simulated radars and has not been checked on real captures.
Distances assume a 105 x 68 m pitch (EA does not publish FC pitch sizes); Rush is played on a smaller pitch and is not measured.
failClosed: Scoreboard unreadable: no goals are counted from score changes.
Non-broadcast camera, menus or replays of other matches: no zones are recorded.
No pitch outline on the radar, a radar hidden for a replay or set piece, or more dots than two teams have: that moment is skipped.
Radar colours left at Default with similar kits, or set to Black: the two teams cannot be told apart, so no team shapes are recorded.
